akhfash:6-7.t: He said ﴿بِعَادٍ﴾ ﴿إِرَمَ﴾, making ﴿إِرَمَ﴾ its name; and some read ﴿بعادِ إِرَمَ﴾, putting it in a genitive construct with ﴿إِرَمَ﴾: either it is the name of their father, to which He annexed them, or a town; and Allah knows best.

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ﴾; and some read ﴿قَدَّرَ﴾, like ﴿قَتَّرَ﴾ ("he stinted"). As for ﴿قَدَرَ﴾, He means: He gives him by measure.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالْفَجْرِ﴾, that is, the dawn of every day,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍ﴾, that is, the ten [nights] of Dhū al-Ḥijja,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَالشَّفْعِ﴾: the even ﴿وَالْوَتْرِ﴾ — with fatḥa and with kasra on the wāw, two dialects — the single,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿هَلْ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ oath ﴿قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ﴾: intellect. The answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is omitted, that is: "You will surely be punished, O disbelievers of Mecca."

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾: know, O Muhammad, ﴿كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ﴾

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِرَمَ﴾: it is the first ʿĀd. So «إرم» is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal (substitute), and it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) because of being a proper name and feminine. ﴿ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ﴾, that is, of tallness: the height of the tallest of them was four hundred cubits,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُهَا فِي الْبِلَادِ﴾ in their might and strength,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جَابُوا﴾: cut ﴿الصَّخْرَ﴾ — plural of «صخرة» — and took them as houses ﴿بِالْوَادِ﴾: Wādī al-Qurā,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتَادِ﴾: he used to drive in four stakes to which he tied the hands and feet of those he tortured,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿فَأَكْثَرُوا فِيهَا الْفَسَادَ﴾: killing and other things.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ﴾: a kind of ﴿عَذَابٍ﴾.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ﴾: He watches over the deeds of the servants, so nothing of them escapes Him, so that He may recompense them for them.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسَانُ﴾, the disbeliever, ﴿إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ﴾: tested him ﴿رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ﴾ with wealth and other things ﴿وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ﴾

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ فَقَدَرَ﴾: restricted ﴿عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَهَانَنِ﴾

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a deterrent (radʿ); that is, honour is not through wealth nor humiliation through poverty, but rather through obedience and disobedience, and the disbelievers of Mecca do not take heed of that. ﴿بَلْ لَا يُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ﴾: they do not treat him well despite their wealth, or they do not give him his due from the inheritance,

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَلَا يَحُضُّونَ﴾ themselves or others ﴿عَلَى طَعَامِ﴾, that is, the feeding of ﴿الْمِسْكِينِ﴾,

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَيَأْكُلُونَ التُّرَاثَ﴾: the inheritance ﴿أَكْلًا لَمًّا﴾, that is, intensely, because they lump together the share of the women and the children in the inheritance with their own share of it, or with their own wealth,

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَيُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا﴾, that is, much, so they do not spend it. In one reading [تُكْرِمُونَ تَحَاضُّونَ تَأْكُلُونَ تُحِبُّونَ], with the upper-dotted letter [tāʾ] in the four verbs.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a deterrent (radʿ) for them from that. ﴿إِذَا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا﴾: is shaken until every building on it collapses and ceases to be,

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَجَاءَ رَبُّكَ﴾, that is, His command, ﴿وَالْمَلَكُ﴾, that is, the angels, ﴿صَفًّا صَفًّا﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, standing in ranks, or possessing many ranks,

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ﴾: it will be led by seventy thousand reins, each rein in the hands of seventy thousand angels, roaring and raging. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: a badal (substitute) from «إذا», and its apodosis (jawāb) is: ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾, that is, the disbeliever, what he neglected. ﴿وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرَى﴾: an interrogative in the sense of negation; that is, his remembering that will not benefit him.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿يَقُولُ﴾ along with his remembering: ﴿يَا﴾ — for calling attention (tanbīh) — ﴿لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ﴾ good and faith ﴿لِحَيَاتِي﴾ — the good life in the Hereafter — or: in the time of my life in this world.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُعَذِّبُ﴾ — with kasra on the dhāl — ﴿عَذَابَهُ﴾, that is, Allah's, ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾, that is, He does not entrust it to anyone else,

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَ﴾ likewise ﴿لَا يُوثِقُ﴾ — with kasra on the thāʾ — ﴿وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ﴾. In one reading it is with fatḥa on the dhāl and the thāʾ; then the pronoun of «عذابه» and «وثاقه» refers to the disbeliever, and the meaning is: no one is punished like his punishment and no one is bound like his binding.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿يَا أَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ﴾: the secure one, which is the believing soul,

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿ارْجِعِي إِلَى رَبِّكِ﴾: this is said to it at death, that is, return to His command and His will, ﴿رَاضِيَةً﴾ with the reward, ﴿مَرْضِيَّةً﴾ with Allah because of your deeds, that is, combining the two descriptions; they are two ḥāls (circumstantials). And it will be said to it at the Resurrection:

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَادْخُلِي فِي﴾ the company of ﴿عِبَادِي﴾ the righteous,

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿وَالْفَجْرِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم" (I swear); ﴿وَلَيالٍ﴾: conjoined to الفجر. ﴿عَشْرٍ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ليال; ﴿وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ﴾: both also conjoined to الفجر; ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾: also conjoined; ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿يَسْرِ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾: a particle of affirmation (taqrīr); ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿قَسَمٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿لِذِي﴾: naʿt (adjective) of قسم; ﴿حِجْرٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is the answer to the oath.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾: the hamza is a particle of affirmative interrogation, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿كَيْفَ﴾: an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿بِعادٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the verbal clause stands in place of the two objects of تر.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إِرَمَ﴾: badal (substitute) for عاد; ﴿ذاتِ﴾: naʿt (adjective), muḍāf to ﴿الْعِمادِ﴾.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿الَّتِي﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of إرم; ﴿لَمْ يُخْلَقْ﴾: لم is a particle of the jussive, and a passive imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; ﴿مِثْلُها﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿فِي الْبِلادِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَثَمُودَ﴾: conjoined to عاد; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ثمود; ﴿جابُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي; ﴿الصَّخْرَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بِالْوادِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَفِرْعَوْنَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿ذِي الْأَوْتادِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of فرعون, muḍāf to الأوتاد.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: badal (substitute) for عاد, ثمود and فرعون; ﴿طَغَوْا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فِي الْبِلادِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿فَأَكْثَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِيهَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْفَسادَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فَصَبَّ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: the Name of Majesty [Translator's note: so in the source], fāʿil (agent); ﴿سَوْطَ عَذابٍ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to عذاب; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصادِ﴾: inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿بالمرصاد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and أما is a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿مَا﴾: redundant (zāʾida); ﴿ابْتَلاهُ﴾: a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿رَبُّهُ﴾: its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿أَكْرَمَنِ﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ of the first person is the direct object; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and أما is a particle of condition and detailing; ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿مَا﴾: redundant (zāʾida); ﴿ابْتَلاهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿رِزْقَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and يقول is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَهانَنِ﴾: a past verb; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ of the first person is the direct object; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿بَلْ﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb); ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿تُكْرِمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الْيَتِيمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: The verse is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَتَأْكُلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿التُّراثَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَكْلًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿لَمًّا﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:20-20.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and its i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke; ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿دُكَّتِ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿الْأَرْضُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); ﴿دَكًّا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); ﴿دَكًّا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq, a tawkīd (emphasis) of what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿وَالْمَلَكُ﴾: conjoined to ربك; ﴿صَفًّا صَفًّا﴾: two ḥāls (circumstantials).

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وَجِيءَ﴾: a passive past verb; ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿بِجَهَنَّمَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and they stand in the place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time annexed to one like it; ﴿يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿أَنَّى﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as the fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar; ﴿الذِّكْرى﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿يَقُولُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿يا﴾: a particle drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿لَيْتَنِي﴾: a particle resembling the verb (one of inna and its sisters); the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is its noun; ﴿قَدَّمْتُ﴾: a past verb and its agent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of layta, and the nominal clause is the maqūl (speech content) of the saying; ﴿لِحَياتِي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and يومئذ is an adverb annexed to one like it; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يُعَذِّبُ﴾: an imperfect verb; ﴿عَذابَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَحَدٌ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:26-26.t: The clause is conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is clear.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿يا أَيَّتُهَا﴾: يا is a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), and ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); ﴿النَّفْسُ﴾: badal (substitute); ﴿الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the vocative clause is the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿ارْجِعِي﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿إِلى رَبِّكِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿راضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً﴾: two ḥāls (circumstantials); the clause is likewise the maqūl (speech content) of an omitted verb of saying.

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿فَادْخُلِي﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿فِي عِبادِي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿وَادْخُلِي﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿جَنَّتِي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الشَّفْعِ) The pair of number. One says: "ashafʿ is it or witr?", i.e. even or odd; its plural is ashfāʿ and shifāʿ. The maṣdar of shafaʿa, yashfaʿu (of the pattern fataḥa) is shafʿ, i.e. he made the thing shafʿ, a pair, by adding its like to it; one says: "it was odd and he paired it (shafaʿahu) with another", i.e. joined it to it. In the Qāmūs: "al-shafʿ is the opposite of al-witr, namely the pair; shafaʿahu, like manaʿahu; and the Day of Aḍḥā. It is said regarding His saying, the Exalted, «والشفع والوتر» that it is creation, because of His saying, the Exalted, «ومن كل شيء خلقنا زوجين», or that it is Allah, mighty and majestic, because of His saying, the Exalted, «ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم»."
(الْوَتْرِ) In the Qāmūs: "al-witr, with kasra or with fatḥa, is the single, or what has not been paired of number; and the Day of ʿArafa."
Abū Ḥayyān said: "'al-Shafʿ and al-witr': it is mentioned in the book al-Taḥrīr wa-l-Taḥbīr that there are thirty-six views about them, which we grew weary of reading, let alone of writing in this book of ours."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "They have said a great deal about the shafʿ and the witr, until they almost exhausted most of what they could fall upon, and that is of very little profit, and deserves to be disregarded."
(حِجْرٍ) Intellect. The intellect is so called because it restrains (yaḥjuru) its owner from what is not lawful or fitting, just as it is called ʿaql because it restrains (yaʿqilu) its owner from vile things and forbids him, and because it forbids what is not lawful or fitting. The root meaning of ḥijr is prevention; this root has been discussed before. Ibn Khālawayh said: "هل في ذلك حجر means: for one who has intellect and understanding." Al-Ḥijr is also the dwellings of Thamūd, the Ḥijr of the Kaʿba, and the female horse.
(جابُوا) They cut through. In al-Mukhtār: "jāba: he pierced and cut through, and its pattern is qāla; of it is His saying, the Exalted, «وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد»; and 'I cut through the lands' (jubtu), with ḍamma on the jīm, of the pattern qāla and bāʿa; and ajabtuhā: I cut through them."

* I'rab:
(وَالْفَجْرِ وَلَيالٍ عَشْرٍ) The واو is a particle of oath and genitive; الفجر is genitive by the oath-wāw, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "I swear"; the واو is a conjunction; and ليال is conjoined to الفجر, genitive, its genitive sign being the fatḥa as a substitute for the kasra implied on the omitted yāʾ, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn Mālik pointed to this important rule in his saying:
وكن لجمع مشبه مفاعلا ... أو المفاعيل بمنع كافلا
(And be, for a plural resembling mafāʿil or al-mafāʿīl, a guarantor of the prohibition [of tanwīn].)
That is, a plural resembling mafāʿil or al-mafāʿīl, in having a fatḥa on the first letter and an alif as the third, followed by two letters like mafāʿil, or three letters whose middle is quiescent like mafāʿīl, is barred from ṣarf because the plural in it stands in place of two causes, namely plurality and the absence of a parallel in the singular. His saying "mafāʿil" includes what begins with a mīm, like masājid, or with another letter, like darāhim; and his saying "al-mafāʿīl" includes what begins with a mīm, like maṣābīḥ, or with another letter, like danānīr. Then, of this plural there is one that comes with a weak final radical, in two kinds. One is that in which the kasra after the alif is turned into fatḥa, so the yāʾ turns into alif, like ʿadhārā, and there is no difficulty in the prohibition of tanwīn. The other is that in which the fatḥa is found heavy in its class and is dropped, and the tanwīn attaches to it; to that he pointed in his saying:
وذا اعتلال منه كالجواري ... رفعا وجرّا أجره كساري
(And what is weak of it, like al-jawārī, in nominative and genitive treat like sārī.)
He means that what is of the plural with a weak final radical, like jawārin, being as described in the dropping of the vowel, is treated like sārin in having tanwīn attached to its end in the nominative and genitive; so you say "hādhihi jawārin" and "marartu bi-jawārin". He kept silent about the accusative, so it is understood that it follows the original rule, like the sound word; so you say "raʾaytu jawāriya".
And عشر is an adjective of ليال. They said that by the ten nights he meant the ten of Dhū l-Ḥijja, and it came indefinite because of their superiority over other nights of the year; it is also said that they are the last ten of Ramaḍān, and that they are the first ten of Muḥarram. (وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَسْرِ) Conjoined to الفجر and ليال, and likewise الوتر and الليل; and إذا is an adverbial attached to the omitted verb of the oath, or to an implied verb of oath, and Abū l-Baqāʾ went that way, i.e. "I swear by the night at the time of its journeying". يسري is an imperfect verb taken from al-sarā, which is particular to journeying by night, and it has been treated before. He said in al-Miṣbāḥ: "saraytu al-layl and saraytu bihi, sarā; the noun is al-sarāya, when you traverse it by traveling; and asraytu, with alif, is a Ḥijāzī dialect; both are used transitively with the bāʾ to an object, so one says 'saraytu bi-Zayd' and 'asraytu bihi'. Al-surya, with ḍamma or fatḥa on the sīn, is more specific; one says 'we journeyed a surya of the night'; the plural is al-surā, like mudya and mudā. Abū Zayd said: al-sarā may be at the beginning of the night, its middle and its end. The Arabs used sarā for abstract things, likening them to bodies, figuratively and by extension. Allah the Exalted said: «والليل إذا يسر», and the meaning is: when it passes. Al-Baghawī said: when it travels and goes. Al-Fārābī said: 'poison and wine and the like sarā in him'. Al-Saraqusṭī said: 'the vein of evil sarā in the human being', and Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ added to that: 'sarā ʿalayhi al-hamm' means it came to him at night, and 'sarā hammuhu' means it went. Ascribing the verb to abstractions is frequent in their speech, such as 'the phantom wandered', 'the worry went', 'sloth and vigor seized him'; and the saying of the jurists 'the wound sarā to the soul' means its pain continued until death resulted from it; and 'his palm was cut off and it sarā to his forearm', i.e. the effect of the wound extended; and 'the prohibition sarā' and 'the emancipation sarā', in the sense of extension. These words are current on the tongues of the jurists, and have no mention in the well-known books, but they are consistent with what preceded." Some of the readers dropped the yāʾ of يسر in pause and kept it in continuation; some kept it in both cases, and some dropped it in both cases because it is absent in the script of the noble codex and to conform to the verse-endings. The wording of Ibn Khālawayh: "The original was yasrī, but they cut short the yāʾ so that it resembles the verse-endings before it; so among the readers there are those who keep the yāʾ according to the original, and those who drop it, following the codex." (هَلْ فِي ذلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ) The sense of the interrogative here is magnification and glorification of the things sworn by; في ذلك is a fronted predicate; قسم is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and لذي حجر is an adjective. On this view هل and what is within its scope are the response to the oath. It is also said that it is for affirmation, as in your saying "Have I not shown you favor?" when you did show favor. The response on this view is omitted, implied, its implied form being "We shall surely requite everyone according to what he did", and al-Zamakhsharī implied "you will surely be punished". It is also said that the response is mentioned, namely «إن ربك لبالمرصاد». The wording of al-Samīn: "Muqātil said: هل here is in the place of إن, its implied form being 'indeed in that is an oath for one of intellect', so هل on this view is in the position of the response to the oath. This is a false statement, because it is not fit to be what is sworn upon, even supposing the construction is so; I mention it only to draw attention to its invalidity." (أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعادٍ، إِرَمَ ذاتِ الْعِمادِ الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُها فِي الْبِلادِ) The hamza is for affirmative interrogation, i.e. "you have seen", because what is meant by seeing here is the seeing of the heart, which is knowledge; it was expressed by seeing because it is necessary knowledge equal in clarity and manifestness to witnessing and eyesight. لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb jussive by لم; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative by a verb, as a maṣdar, and al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn Hishām in al-Mughnī preferred it; the meaning is: "what action did your Lord do". Ibn Khālawayh parsed it as ḥāl; he said: "كيف is a question about the state." But that is impermissible, because if it is parsed as ḥāl it would be from the agent, and describing Him, the Exalted, with modality is impossible and not allowed. The clause suspended by the interrogative كيف takes the place of the two objects of تر. فعل ربك is a past verb and an agent; وبعاد are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to فعل; and إرم is a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of عاد, and is barred from ṣarf for being a proper name and feminine. This substitution is a notification that they are the first, ancient ʿĀd. It is also said that Iram is their city or their land in which they were. The wording of Abū l-Baqāʾ: "Iram is not declined because of definiteness and femininity. It is said it is the name of a tribe; on that view the implied form is 'Iram, the owner of ذات العماد', because ذات العماد is a city. It is also said that ذات العماد is a description, as you say 'the tribe possessing kingship'. It is also said that Iram is a city; on that view the implied form is 'ʿĀd, the owner of Iram'. It is read بعاد إرم by annexation, requiring no implication, and it is read إرم ذات العماد with genitive by
annexation." ذات العماد is an adjective of إرم, i.e. of tallness. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "ذات العماد, if it is a description of the tribe, means that they were bedouins, people of tent-poles, or tall in body, likening their stature to pillars; of it is the saying 'a muʿmad man' and 'ʿummadān' when he is tall. It is also said: possessing lofty building. If it is a description of the city, the meaning is that it has columns." A summary of its wonderful story will come in the section of Benefits. التي is a second adjective of إرم; the clause لم يخلق is the ṣila of التي; مثلها is the deputy agent of يخلق; and في البلاد are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to يخلق. It was read يخلق in the active, in which case مثلها is a direct object. (وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جابُوا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوادِ) The واو is a conjunction; ثمود is conjoined to عاد; الذين is an adjective of ثمود; the clause جابوا is the ṣila of الذين; الصخر is a direct object; and بالوادي are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to جابوا, the باء being locative, hence meaning "in"; the yāʾ was dropped because it is one of the supplementary yāʾs. (وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتادِ) Conjoined to عاد; and ذي الأوتاد is an adjective of فرعون: he used to drive four stakes for the one he tortured, and bind him with them stretched on the ground, and then torture him as he wished, by beating, burning and other means. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "al-watid, with kasra on the tāʾ, in the dialect of the Ḥijāz, which is the most eloquent, and its plural is awtād; with fatḥa on the tāʾ is a dialect; the people of Najd put sukūn on the tāʾ and assimilate after the conversion, leaving wadd. watadtu al-watid, atidu, watdan (of the pattern waʿada): I fixed it in a wall or the ground; and awtadtuhu, with alif, is a dialect." (الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلادِ فَأَكْثَرُوا فِيهَا الْفَسادَ) الذين is either genitive as an adjective of those mentioned or accusative in censure. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The best of the views on it is that it be in the position of accusative in censure; it may be nominative, as 'they are those who transgressed', or genitive, describing those mentioned: ʿĀd, Thamūd and Pharaoh." The clause طغوا is the ṣila of الذين, and في البلاد are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to طغوا. (فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذابٍ) The فاء is a conjunction; صبّ is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; عليهم are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to صبّ; ربك is the agent; and سوط عذاب is a direct object. The meaning of this expression will come in the section of Rhetoric. (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصادِ) The clause has no position, because it is a justification for what precedes; إن and its noun; the shifted lām; and بالمرصاد are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to an omitted word that is the predicate of إن. Its meaning too will come in the section of Rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «فصبّ عليهم ربك سوط عذاب» is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). He used "pouring", which is particular to water, because it requires swiftness in descent upon the one struck. He said:
فصبّ عليهم محصرات كأنها ... شآبيب ليست من سحاب ولا قطر
(So He poured on them besieging [showers], as though they were downpours that were neither from cloud nor rain.)
And another said, describing horses:
صببنا عليهم ظالمين سياطنا ... فطارت بها أيد سراع وأرجل
(We poured on them, unjustly, our whips, and swift hands and legs flew with them.)
He borrowed the whip for the punishment because it requires of repetition and recurrence what the sword and others do not. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī is beautiful of its kind. He said: "One says: 'he poured the whip on him', 'covered him with it' and 'hooded him with it'. The mention of the whip is an indication that what He sent down upon them in this world of great punishment, measured against what He has prepared for them in the next, is like the whip when measured against everything else with which one is tortured." Al-sawṭ, as in the Qāmūs, is mixing, or that you mix two things in your vessel and then beat them with your hand until they mix, like al-taswīṭ; and the whip because it mixes flesh with blood; the plural is siyāṭ and aswāṭ. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is a word the Arabs say for every kind of punishment. The origin of that is that the whip is their punishment with which they are tortured, so it came to be used for every punishment when it is at the extreme of punishment."
2- In His saying «إن ربك لبالمرصاد» is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya). He likened the Exalted's being keeper of the deeds of servants, watching over them and requiting what is small and great of them, so that none escapes Him in any case, to one who sits on the road lying in wait for whoever travels it, to seize him and do to him what he wishes; then the word of one of them was applied to the other.

* Benefits:
The Qur'anic story, in its subject, its manner of presentation, its choice of events and the sequence of its scenes, submitted to the requirements of religious purposes, and the traces of this submission appeared in many features. But this complete submission to religious purposes, and its fulfilling this purpose in full, did not prevent the artistic characteristics from standing out in its presentation, especially in depiction, which is the most prominent characteristic of the Qur'an. We would have liked to transmit to you the story of Dhāt al-ʿImād as the narrators and exegetes transmitted it, but the matter would be long, so it suffices us to transmit its summary, that you may glimpse in its light its artistic characteristics, and then refer you to the longer works. They narrated that ʿĀd had two sons, Shaddād and Shadīd, who ruled and prevailed; then Shadīd died and the matter fell wholly to Shaddād, who ruled the world and whose kings submitted to him. He heard of the mention of Paradise and said: "I shall build the like of it." So he built Iram in one of the deserts of ʿAdan over three hundred years, and his age was nine hundred years. It is a great city, upon which imagination bestowed marvels of wonderful description: its palaces of gold and silver, its columns of chrysolite and ruby, and in it were all kinds of trees and flowing rivers. When its building was complete, he set out toward it with the people of his kingdom; when he was a day and a night's journey away, Allah sent upon them a cry from the sky and they perished. It is reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qilāba that he went out seeking camels of his, and happened upon it, and carried off what he could of what was there. His news reached Muʿāwiya, who summoned him, and he told him; he sent to Kaʿb and asked him, and he said: "It is Iram Dhāt al-ʿImād, and a man of the Muslims will enter it in your time, ruddy, fair-haired, short, with a mole on his brow and a mole on his heel, who goes out seeking camels of his." Then he turned and saw Ibn Abī Qilāba and said: "By Allah, this is that man." In any case, this has no religious basis to rely on, and various superstitions have been introduced and fabricated tales and contrived legends woven into the exegesis of the Book of Allah, glory be to Him.

dervis-irab:15-30.t:
* Vocabulary:
(التُّراثَ) Inheritance; the tāʾ is a substitute for wāw because it is from wirātha (inheriting), as they said in tujāh, tukhma and tukaʾa.
(لَمًّا) Gathering, devouring. In al-Mukhtār: "akl lammā of the thing he did, of the pattern radda; one says: 'Allah gathered (lamma) his disorder', i.e. He set right and gathered what was scattered of his affair." Abū ʿUbayda said: "lamamtu what was on the table when I ate everything on it entirely." Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
إذا كان لما يتبع الذّم ربه ... فلا قدّس الرحمن تلك الطواحنا
(If devouring is what disgrace follows in its owner, then may the Merciful not sanctify those grinders.)
And of it is lamamtu al-shaʿth (I gathered the disorder). Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
ولست بمستبق أخا لا تلمه ... على شعث أيّ الرجال المهذب
(You will not keep a brother whom you do not set right in his disorder; which man is refined?)
(وَثاقَهُ) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "wathuqa al-shayʾ, with ḍamma, wathāqatan: it was strong and firm, so it is wathīq, firm; awthaqtuhu: I made it firm; and al-wathāq, with fatḥa or kasra on the wāw, is the fetter, the rope and the like; the plural is wuthuq, like ribāṭ and ribuṭ."

* I'rab:
(فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسانُ إِذا مَا ابْتَلاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ) The فاء is resumptive, though the sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that it is a conjunction. He said: "If you say: to what is His saying 'As for man' connected? I say: to His saying «إن ربك لبالمرصاد», as though it were said: 'Allah wants from man only obedience and striving for the outcome, and He lies in wait with punishment for the disobedient; as for man, he does not want that, and is concerned only with the immediate world and what pleases and comforts him in it.'" In his words there is a clear Muʿtazilite whiff. أما is a particle of condition and elaboration; الإنسان is a mubtadaʾ; إذا is an adverbial attached to يقول; ما is redundant; the clause ابتلاه is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; ربه is the agent; فأكرمه is conjoined to ابتلاه; ونعمه is also conjoined; the فاء is a linker because of the sense of condition in أما; and the clause يقول is the khabar of الإنسان. The adverbial's attachment to يقول, which occurs as a predicate, is not precluded, because the adverbial is intended to be postponed, the implied form being: "as for man, he is one who says 'my Lord has honored me' at the time of testing." ربي is a mubtadaʾ and the clause أكرمني is the khabar; they dropped the yāʾ from أكرمن for brevity. (وَأَمَّا إِذا مَا ابْتَلاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَهانَنِ) Conjoined to the preceding clause, and its parsing is like its parsing. (كَلَّا بَلْ لا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ وَلا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلى طَعامِ الْمِسْكِينِ) كلا is a particle of rebuke and reproach to man for his saying; بل is a particle of iḍrāb (turning away) from the ugly to the uglier, to progress in their censure; لا is negative; تكرمون اليتيم is an imperfect verb, nominative, with an agent and a direct object; ولا تحاضّون is conjoined to لا تكرمون; and على طعام المسكين are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to تحاضّون. (وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّراثَ أَكْلًا لَمًّا وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا) Also conjoined; التراث is the object of تأكلون; أكلا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and لما is an adjective; and تحبون المال حبّا جمّا is also conjoined, like the preceding clause in parsing. (كَلَّا إِذا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا) كلا is a particle of rebuke and reproach to them for all that; إذا is an adverbial attached to يتذكر; the clause دكّت is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it; الأرض is the deputy agent; and دكّا دكّا are two maṣdars in the position of ḥāl according to the opinion of Abū Ḥayyān and al-Zamakhsharī, the second not being emphasis; rather the repetition indicates comprehensiveness, as in "I read grammar chapter by chapter". Ibn Khālawayh parsed the first دكّا as a maṣdar and the second as emphasis, which is not remote. (وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا) Conjoined to what preceded; وجاء ربك is a verb and an agent; الملك is conjoined to ربك; and صفّا صفّا is a ḥāl, i.e. "in rows" or "possessing rows". What allows the ḥāl to come as a non-derived noun is the sequence (tartīb), whose rule is that elaboration comes after mention of the whole in its two parts repeated. Al-Raḍī said: there is disagreement about the accusative of the second part: al-Zajjāj held that it is emphasis; Ibn Jinnī held that it is an adjective; al-Fārisī held that it is accusative by the first, because when it took the place of the ḥāl it could operate. Al-Murādī said: the preferred view is that it and what precedes it are accusative by the first operative, because the two together are the ḥāl, and its parallel in predicates is "this is sweet-sour". If someone held that its accusative is by conjunction with the فاء omitted in implication, the meaning being "bāban fa-bāban" and "ṣaffan fa-ṣaffan", it would be a good view. Abū l-Ḥasan stated explicitly that a conjunction particle may not enter any of the repeated items except the فاء, specifically. (وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسانُ وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرى) The واو is a conjunction; جيء is a past passive verb; يومئذ is an adverbial annexed to its like, attached to جيء; بجهنم is in the position of nominative as deputy agent; the second يومئذ is an adverbial annexed to its like and is a badal (substitute) for إذا; the clause يتذكر الإنسان has no position because it is the response to إذا; the واو is a ḥāl-wāw; أنى is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of accusative as an adverbial of place, attached to an omitted fronted predicate; وله are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to what the adverbial is attached to; and الذكرى is a postponed mubtadaʾ. An omitted muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "and from where would he have the benefit of the reminder", otherwise there would be contradiction and inconsistency between "he remembers" and "how could he have the reminder". (يَقُولُ: يا لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي) The clause is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for the clause يتذكر, or a resumption that came as an answer to a question arising from it, as though it were said "What does he say upon his remembering?", and it was said "He says". يا is a particle of alert, or the one addressed is omitted; ليتني: ليت and its noun; the clause قدمت is its predicate; ولحياتي are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to قدمت; and the vocative clause is the content of the saying. (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ وَلا يُوثِقُ وَثاقَهُ أَحَدٌ) The فاء is a conjunction; يومئذ is an adverbial attached to يعذب, and the tanwīn is a compensation for a clause that conveys the preceding terror of the situation; لا is negative; يعذب is an active imperfect verb; عذابه is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the pronoun in عذابه refers to Allah
. It is surprising of Ibn Khālawayh that he parsed it as a direct object, and I do not know what his viewpoint is. أحد is the agent of يعذب. It was read يعذَّب in the passive, in which case أحد is the deputy agent and the pronoun in عذابه refers to the unbeliever. The wording of al-Qurṭubī on this point: "«فيومئذ لا يعذب عذابه أحد», i.e. no one punishes like Allah's punishment, and no one binds like His binding, the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, and this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan. Al-Kisāʾī read لا يعذَّب ولا يوثَق with fatḥa on the dhāl and the thāʾ, i.e. no one is punished in this world like Allah's punishment of the unbeliever on that day, and none is bound as the unbeliever is bound." His saying ولا يوثق etc. is conjoined to the preceding clause, and what was said in parsing the first is said about it. Ibn Khālawayh cited an interesting discussion which we quote here: "'ولا يوثق' is a conjunction upon يعذب; the maṣdar is awthaqa, yūthiqu, īthāqan, so he is mūthaq. If someone says: is it permissible to pronounce yūthiq with hamza as yuʾmin is pronounced with hamza? Say: that is not permissible, because in awthaqa the fāʾ of the verb [first radical] is like awfaḍa, yūfiḍu, asraʿa, yusriʿu, awrā, yūrī, and awqada, yūqidu, all of which are without hamza. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: «إلى نصب يوفضون» and «النار التي تورون». The hamza is pronounced only in those whose first radical is a hamza, such as āmana, yuʾminu, because the original is aʾmana, and they found two hamzas at the beginning of a word heavy, so the second was softened; so know that. If the first radical is a yāʾ, like aysara, ayqana and ayfaʿa al-ghulām, the yāʾ is turned into wāw in the imperfect because of the ḍamma before it and its quiescence, and it is also not permissible to pronounce it with hamza, as in yūqinūna, yūfiʿu al-ghulām and yūsiru. Abū l-Ḥasan the reciter told me: Abū Khalīfa al-Baṣrī narrated from al-Māzinī from al-Akhfash, who said: I heard Abū Ḥayya al-Numayrī say 'yuʾqinūn' with hamza; and Abū Ḥayya is the one who says:
إذا مضغت بعد امتناع من الضحى ... أنابيب من عود الأراك المخلّق
سقت شعب المسواك ماء غمامة ... فضيضا بجادي العراق المروّق
(When, after the height of forenoon has passed, she chews pieces of perfumed arāk wood, the toothstick's strands are watered with cloud-water, flowing, scented with saffron of Iraq, clarified.)
However, some of the Arabs pronounce with hamza what is not pronounced with hamza, likening it to what is, as in their saying 'ḥalaʾtu al-sawīq' and 'rathaʾtu al-mayyit'. Aḥmad told me from ʿAlī from Abū ʿUbayda, who said: al-Ḥasan read «ولا أدرأكم به» with hamza, and it is a mistake according to the grammarians, because it is from darayt." (يا أَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ، ارْجِعِي إِلى رَبِّكِ راضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً) The clause is in the position of accusative by an omitted "saying", i.e. "Allah says to the believer". يا is a particle of vocative; أية is an indefinite specified one addressed, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and parallels have occurred often; the هاء is for alert; النفس is a badal (substitute); المطمئنة is an adjective of النفس; ارجعي is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ is the agent; وإلى ربك are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to ارجعي; and راضية مرضية are two ḥāls. (فَادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي وَادْخُلِي جَنَّتِي) In sequence upon ارجعي; وفي عبادي are two [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to ادخلي; and وادخلي جنتي is also conjoined, i.e. "enter into their ranks and enter My Paradise with them."

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وجاء ربك والملك صفّا صفّا» is the art of excess in description (ifrāṭ fī l-ṣifa), as Ibn al-Muʿtazz named it; Qudāma named it mubālagha (hyperbole), others named it tablīgh, and Qudāma's naming is the well-known one. He defined it by saying: it is that the speaker mentions a state which, were he to stop at it, would suffice, but he does not stop at it until he adds in his speech what is more eloquent in the meaning he intends. It has various kinds, among them putting the speech in the form of reporting of the greatest, mightiest, for hyperbole, while the report about him is figurative, as the saying of someone who sees a great procession or a vast army, "The king himself has come", while knowing that what has come is his army. In the verse He made the coming of the mightiest of His signs a coming of Himself, glory be to Him.

* Benefits:
1- أيها and أيتها: the majority read «يا أيتها النفس» with the feminine tāʾ, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read يا أيها without tāʾ. We know of no one who mentioned that it may be masculine even when the one addressed is feminine except the author of al-Badīʿ, and this verse is witness to that. There is an analogical reason for it: since it is not dualized or pluralized in addressing duals and plurals, so it is not made masculine in addressing the feminine either. أي and أية are indeclinable on the ḍamma because each is a single one addressed, and the alerting hāʾ in them is redundant and inseparable from the word, i.e. and أية as a compensation for the muḍāf ilayhi, with fatḥa on the hāʾ.
2- How dakhala is made transitive: when what is entered is not a true container (ẓarf), dakhala is made transitive to it by في, as in "I entered into the matter" and "I entered into the throng of people", and of it is «فادخلي في عبادي», i.e. among My righteous servants; and when what is entered is a true container, it is generally transitive to it without the mediation of في, and of it is «وادخلي جنتي». In any case جنتي is parsed as a direct object by extension, because in origin it is not transitive by itself, as has preceded.

farraa:1-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْفَجْرِ﴾ ﴿وَلَيالٍ عَشْرٍ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying]: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd concerning His saying: ﴿وَٱلْفَجْرِ﴾. He said: it is this dawn of yours. ﴿وَلَيالٍ عَشْرٍ﴾: he said: the ten [days] of al-Aḍḥā. ﴿وَٱلشَّفْعِ﴾: the day of al-Aḍḥā; and ﴿وَٱلْوَتْرِ﴾: the day of ʿArafa.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying]: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And a shaykh narrated to me from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān from ʿAṭāʾ: [regarding what] Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: the odd and the even are His creation.
He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And a shaykh narrated to me from Layth from Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the odd is Adam; he was made even (paired) by his wife. The readers differed over الوتر: al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read: الوِتر with kasra on the wāw, and so did Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Sulamī, ʿĀṣim and the people of Medina read "الوَتر" with fatḥa on the wāw, and it is a Ḥijāzi dialect.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ﴾.
They mentioned that it is the night of al-Muzdalifa. The readers have read: "يسري" with the yāʾ retained, and "يسر" with it dropped. Dropping it is dearer to me because it matches the verse-endings, and because the Arabs sometimes drop the yāʾ and make do with the kasra of what precedes it. Someone recited to me:
كفّاكَ كفٌّ ما تُلِيقُ دِرْهَماً * جوداً، وأخرى تُعطِ بالسيف الدِّما
(Your two hands: one hand that out of generosity holds on to no dirham, and another that gives [تعطِ for تعطي] blood with the sword.)
And another recited to me:
ليس تَخفَى يسارتى قدر يوم * ولقد تَخفِ شيمتى إعسارى
(My ease does not stay hidden for the space of a day, yet my nature does hide [تخفِ for تخفي] my hardship.)

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ فِي ذَلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِّذِى حِجْرٍ﴾.
For one of intellect; for one of restraint (sitr). All of it goes back to one thing: intellect. The Arabs say: إنه لذو حجر (he is a man of ḥijr) when he masters himself and controls it; as though it was taken from your saying: حجرت على الرجل (I put the man under restriction).

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He [136/b]: ﴿إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلْعِمَادِ﴾.
The readers did not decline (إرم) as a triptote because, according to what they mentioned, it is the name of a town. Al-Kalbī mentioned with his isnad that (إرم) is Sām ibn Nūḥ; if it is a name in this way, its declension was left only because it is like a foreign [name]. (إرم) follows عاد [as its apposition]. (العماد): they were people of [tent-]poles who moved to wherever the pasture was, then returned to their dwellings.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿جَابُواْ ٱلصَّخْرَ﴾: they hollowed out the rock and took it as houses.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِى ٱلأَوْتَادِ﴾.
When he was angry with a man, he would stretch him between four stakes until he died in torment; and he did that to his wife Āsiya bint Muzāḥim. So he was called by this because of that.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ﴾.
This is an expression the Arabs use for every kind of punishment, bringing the whip (السوط) into it; speech and proverb have run with it.
We consider that this is because the whip was among the punishments with which they were punished, so it came to be used for every punishment, since for them it held the utmost of punishment.

farraa:14-14.t: His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ﴾. He says: to Him is the return.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and the general body of readers read it lightened; Nāfiʿ [?] and Abū Jaʿfar read: (فقدّر), with shadda, meaning (فقتّر) (He stinted); and both are correct.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ﴾.
It was not fitting for him to be like this; rather he should praise Him for both matters: for wealth and for poverty.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read it with alif and fatḥa on the tāʾ; the people of Medina read: "ولا تَحُضّون"; al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read: "ويحُضّون، ويأكلون"; and some read: "تُحاضّون" with ḍamma on the tāʾ. All are correct.
It is as though "تُحاضّون" means: you take care [of it]; "تَحُضّون": you command that he be fed; and تَحاضّون: you urge one another [137/a].

farraa:19-20.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَكْلاً لَّمًّا﴾: a voracious eating; ﴿وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلْمَالَ حُبّاً جَمّاً﴾: abundant.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَقُولُ يٰلَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي﴾.
For my Hereafter, in which there is life and everlastingness.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and the people of Medina read: "لا يعذِّب عذابَه أحدٌ، ولا يُوثِقُ", both with kasra.
Ḥamza read it so. [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us], saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: And ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak narrated to me from Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ from Abū Qilāba from someone who heard the Prophet ﷺ reading: "فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُعذَّب عذابَه أَحَدٌ، ولا يُوثَق وَثاقَه أَحَد", with fatḥa. [Abū ʿAbd Allāh] Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm said: I heard ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Khaffāf [relate] the same with this isnad. [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us.]
He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak narrated to me from Sulaymān Abū al-Rabīʿ from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī that he read: "لا يُعذِّبُ عَذَابَه أَحَدٌ، ولا يُوثِقُ", with kasra. Whoever reads with kasra means: on that Day no one punishes as Allah punishes. Whoever says "يُعذَّب" with fatḥa, it is also on that interpretation: no one is punished in this world like the punishment of Allah on that Day. Likewise the first interpretation: you do not see anyone punishing in this world like the punishment of Allah on that Day. Some have interpreted it as [referring to] a specific man: no one is punished as he is punished.

farraa:27-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيَّتُهَا ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ﴾.
[At peace] in faith, and affirming the reward and the resurrection. ﴿ٱرْجِعِي﴾: the angels say [this] to them when they are given their records in their right hands: ﴿ٱرْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ﴾, to the reward that Allah has prepared for you. It may also be that they say this to them intending: return from this world to this destination. You say to a man: "Whom are you from?" and he says: "I am of Muḍar."
Then you say: "Be a Tamīmī or a Qaysī", i.e. you are from one of these two. So "كن" (be) is a ṣila (i.e. it adds nothing), and likewise the returning [137/b] is a ṣila, because he has already come to the Resurrection; so it is as though the command has the meaning of a statement, as though He said: O soul, you are well-pleased, well-pleasing.
Ibn ʿAbbās alone read: "فادخلى فى عبدى، وادخلى جنتى" (enter into My servant [i.e. his body] and enter My Garden), while the general public read (فى عبادى) (among My servants).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: (وليال عشر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] A noun conjoined to «الفجر», genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ; the fatḥa was implied only because it stands in for the kasra; «عشر»: naʿt (adjective), genitive; and the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is omitted, i.e.: We will surely recompense everyone for what he did, as evidenced by His enumeration of what He did to the bygone generations.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «إذا»: a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of the oath; «يَسْرِ»: imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ; and the clause «يسر» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The preposition «في ذلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «قسم»; «لذي» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «قسم»; and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «كيف فعل» stands in place of the two objects of the seeing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; «كيف» is an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «التي»: naʿt (adjective) of {ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ}; the preposition «في البلاد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يخلق».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: His saying «وثمود»: a noun conjoined to «عاد», genitive (majrūr) with fatḥa because it is a diptote, on account of being a proper name and feminine; «الذين»: naʿt (adjective); «بالواد»: a noun, genitive with the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ; the preposition «بالواد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جابوا».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: His saying «وفرعون»: conjoined to «ثمود»; «ذي»: naʿt (adjective), genitive (majrūr).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «الذين»: naʿt (adjective) of «فرعون», with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: the people of Pharaoh.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «فأكثروا» is conjoined to the clause {طَغَوْا}.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «فصبَّ» is conjoined to the clause «أكثروا».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: (إن ربك لبالمرصاد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «أما»: a particle of condition and detailing; the conditional clause is parenthetical; «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the implied apodosis; «ما»: redundant (zāʾida); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer of «أمَّا», which is the khabar (predicate) of «الإنسان»; the clause «فيقول» is the khabar of «الإنسان», and the fāʾ is the linking one; «أكرمن»: past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, the nūn is that of protection (wiqāya), and the implied yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: (وأما إذا ما ابتلاه فقدر عليه رزقه فيقول ربي أهانن) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the preceding one; the mubtadaʾ (subject) after «أمَّا» is implied (muqaddar), and the i'rab is as given in the previous verse.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «حبا»: a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), so it is nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يَتَذَكَّرُ}; «دكا دكا»: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being: the pounding being repeated upon it, as in "I taught him arithmetic chapter by chapter"; the second is not tawkīd (emphasis).

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «صفًا صفًا»: ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: standing in ranks; and the clause «جاء» is conjoined to {دُكَّتِ}.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The clause «وجيء» is conjoined to the clause {دُكَّتِ}, and the preposition «بجهنم» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «يومئذ»: badal (substitute) of {إِذَا}; the second «يومئذ»: badal of the first; and the clause «يتذكر» is the apodosis (jawāb) of {إِذَا} in verse (21). The wāw in «وأنى» is parenthetical; «أنى»: an interrogative noun, an adverb meaning "from where", attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «الذكرى» is mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition «له» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذكرى».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «يقول» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from the clause {يَتَذَكَّرُ}; «يا» is for alerting (tanbīh).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «يومئذ»: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يعذب»; «أحد» is a fāʿil (agent) placed later

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «وثاقه» is nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq (substitute for the absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The clause «ارجعي» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive; «راضية مرضية» are two ḥāls (circumstantials).

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The clause «فادخلي» is conjoined to the clause {ارْجِعِي}.

mekki-muskil:6-7.t: His saying, the Exalted: (بعاد إرم): (إرم) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of (عاد), or as a badal (substitute); the meaning of (إرم) is "the ancient". Whoever makes (إرم) a city assumes an omission in the speech, its implied form being "with the city of ʿĀd, Iram". It is also said that its implied form is "with ʿĀd, the owner of Iram"; on this view (إرم) is a definite feminine noun, which is why it is a diptote. (عاد) is fully declinable because it is masculine and light. It has been said that Iram is a great city existing at this time; it is also said that it is Alexandria, and also said that it is Damascus.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying (صفا صفا): a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying (وثمود الذين): [(ثمود)] is a diptote because it is the name of the tribe and is definite; its position is genitive by conjunction with (عاد). (الذين) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of (ثمود), or in the position of the accusative with "I mean" (أعني), or in the position of the nominative with an implied (هم).
His saying (ولا يحضون على طعام المسكين): the object of (يحضون) is omitted, its implied form being "and they do not urge people", or "themselves", or the like, "to feed the poor". Whoever reads it (تحاضون) does not assume the omission of an object; it is only "you urge one another among yourselves to good", and it is intransitive. [Translator's note: these comments concern verses 15–18 and 20 although the entry is keyed to verse 22; translated as written.]

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying (وجيء يومئذ بجهنم): (بجهنم) is in the position of the nominative as the object whose agent is not named [nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. It is also said that the maṣdar (verbal noun) is implied and is the object whose agent is not named. It may also be that the [deputy] object is (يومئذ).
His saying (يومئذ): a badal (substitute) from the first one. It is also said that its governor is (يتذكر).
His saying (وأنى له الذكرى): [(الذكرى)] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أنى) is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿فأما﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing, indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿الإنسان﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, indeclinable on the sukūn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقول﴾.
﴿ما﴾: a connective (ṣila) particle, indeclinable on the sukūn, with no grammatical position.
﴿ابتلاه﴾: «ابتلى» is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, its appearance prevented by impossibility, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿ابتلاه﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer of ﴿أما﴾.
﴿ربه﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فأكرمه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and «أكرمه» is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿فأكرمه﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ابتلاه﴾, in the position of genitive.
﴿ونعمه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa [Translator's note: so in the source; the conjunction in ﴿ونعمه﴾ is the wāw], and «نعمه» is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿ونعمه﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ابتلاه﴾, in the position of genitive.
﴿فيقول﴾: the fāʾ is a linking fāʾ (rābiṭa) because of the conditional sense in ﴿أما﴾, and «يقول» is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause «يقول» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿الإنسان﴾.
﴿ربي﴾: mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied on the letter before the yāʾ because the place is occupied by the vowel of harmony, and the yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أكرمن﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the nūn is of protection (al-wiqāya), a particle indeclinable on the kasra with no grammatical position, and the omitted yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿أكرمني﴾ is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ربي﴾, the clause ﴿ربي أكرمن﴾ is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause ﴿فأما الإنسان...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وأما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «أما» is a particle of condition and detailing, indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, indeclinable on the sukūn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقول﴾.
﴿ما﴾: a connective (ṣila) particle, indeclinable on the sukūn, with no grammatical position.
﴿ابتلاه﴾: «ابتلى» is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, its appearance prevented by impossibility, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿ابتلاه﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.
﴿فقدر﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and ﴿قدر﴾ is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿قدر﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ابتلاه﴾, in the position of genitive.
﴿عليه﴾: «على» is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the kasra in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿قدر﴾.
﴿رزقه﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿فيقول﴾: the fāʾ is a linking fāʾ (rābiṭa) because of the conditional sense in ﴿أما﴾, and ﴿يقول﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the agent is latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو); the clause ﴿يقول﴾ is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he" (هو).
﴿ربي﴾: mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied on the letter before the yāʾ because the place is occupied by the vowel of harmony, and the yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أهانن﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; the nūn is of protection (al-wiqāya), a particle indeclinable on the kasra with no grammatical position, and the omitted yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿أهانن﴾ is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ربي﴾, the nominal clause is the answer of ﴿إذا﴾, and the clause of «إذا» with its condition and its answer is in the position of nominative as khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "man" (الإنسان).

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿بل﴾: a particle of digression (iḍrāb), indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿لا﴾: negating, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿تكرمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿اليتيم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿لا تكرمون...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «لا» is negating, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿تحاضون﴾: conjoined to ﴿تكرمون﴾; an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿على﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿طعام﴾: a noun in the genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تحاضون﴾.
﴿المسكين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural. [Translator's note: so in the source; ﴿المسكين﴾ is singular and its genitive sign is the kasra.]

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وتأكلون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «تأكلون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿التراث﴾: the object of «تأكلون», accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿أكلا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿لما﴾: an adjective (ṣifa), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa. The clause is conjoined to «لا تكرمون».

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿وتحبون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «تحبون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿المال﴾: the object of «تحبون», accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿حبًّا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿جمًّا﴾: an adjective (ṣifa), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause is conjoined to «لا تكرمون».

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, indeclinable on the sukūn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتذكر﴾ in the saying of the Exalted ﴿يومئذ يتذكر الإنسان﴾.
﴿دكت﴾: a past verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the tāʾ is of the feminine, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿الأرض﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿دكا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿دكا﴾: verbal tawkīd (emphasis), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause «دكت الأرض» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿وجاء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «جاء» is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿ربك﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿والملك﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and «الملك» is a noun conjoined to ﴿ربك﴾, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿صفا صفا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa, i.e. "ranged in rows" (مصطفين), or "possessing rows" (ذوي صفوف); or the first «صفًّا» is a ḥāl and the second is an adjective (ṣifa), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa; or it is made accusative by the first; or it is conjoined to the first with an omitted fāʾ understood, i.e. «صفا فصفًّا» ("row upon row"); or it is tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿وجاء﴾ is conjoined to ﴿دكت﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿وجيء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «جيء» is a past verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جيء﴾; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable on the sukūn, implied because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿بجهنم﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition indeclinable on the kasra, and «جهنم» is a noun in the genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿يومئذ﴾: «يوم» is an adverb, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, and it is a badal (substitute) for ﴿إذا دكت﴾, attached to ﴿يتذكر﴾; and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable on the sukūn, implied because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿يتذكر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿الإنسان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿يتذكر﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of ﴿إذا﴾.
﴿وأنى﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), a particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, or parenthetical. «أنى» is an interrogative noun meaning negation, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, and it is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿له﴾: the lām is a preposition indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the fronted khabar.
﴿الذكرى﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied, its appearance prevented by impossibility; an omitted muḍāf must be understood, i.e. "and whence will he have the benefit of the remembrance" (ومن أين له منفعة الذكرى). The clause ﴿أنى له الذكرى﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الإنسان», or it is a parenthetical clause.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿يقول﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿يا﴾: a particle of alerting, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, or a vocative particle with the one addressed omitted.
﴿ليتني﴾: «ليت» is an abrogating particle indeclinable on the fatḥa, the nūn is of protection (al-wiqāya), a particle indeclinable on the kasra, and the yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of accusative as the noun (ism) of ﴿ليت﴾.
﴿قدمت﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿قدمت﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ﴿ليت﴾.
﴿لحياتي﴾: the lām is a preposition indeclinable on the kasra, and «حياتي» is a noun in the genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and the yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قدمت﴾; the clause ﴿يا ليتني﴾ is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause ﴿يقول...﴾ is resumptive by way of explanation (bayāniyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿فيومئذ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; in ﴿يومئذ﴾, «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the negated verb ﴿يعذب﴾, and «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable on the sukūn, implied because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied wording being: "on the day when the states and sayings mentioned come to pass, none will punish" (يوم إذ يكون ما ذُكر من الأحوال والأقوال لا يعذب).
﴿لا﴾: negating, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿يعذب﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿عذابه﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أحد﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «لا» is connective (ṣila), for emphasising the negation.
﴿يوثق﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma.
﴿وثاقه﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أحد﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause ﴿لا يوثق﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لا يعذب﴾.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿أيتها﴾: «أية» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative, and «ها» is for alerting, a particle indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿النفس﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أية﴾.
﴿المطمئنة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نفس﴾, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma; the clause is in the place of accusative by an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "Allah says to ﴿المؤمن﴾ (the believer)".

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿ارجعي﴾: an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلى﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿ربك﴾: a noun in the genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ارجعي﴾.
﴿راضية﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿مرضية﴾: a second ḥāl from the agent, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa; the clause ﴿ارجعي﴾ is the answer to the vocative, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿فادخلي﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «ادخلي» is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ of the addressee is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿في﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿عبادي﴾: a noun in the genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the kasra, and the yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ادخلي﴾; the clause ﴿ادخلي﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ارجعي﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿وادخلي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and «ادخلي» is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the yāʾ of the addressee is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿جنتي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ, its appearance prevented by the place being occupied by the vowel of harmony, and the yāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿ادخلي﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ارجعي﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿والفجر﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and al-fajr is a noun in the genitive by the wāw of the oath, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقسم﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وليال﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and layālin is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to al-fajr, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa standing in for the kasra, implied (muqaddar) on the dropped yāʾ.
﴿عشر﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ليال﴾, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿والشفع﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and al-shafʿ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿الفجر﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿والوتر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable on the fatḥa, and al-watr is conjoined to ﴿الفجر﴾, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿والليل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and al-layl is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿الفجر﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of the future indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ﴿أقسم﴾.
﴿يسر﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ, which is dropped to match the ends of the ayahs.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿هل﴾: an interrogative noun [Translator's note: so in the source; hal is normally classed as an interrogative particle] indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
﴿في﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿ذلك﴾: dhā is a demonstrative indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the lām is for distance, a particle indeclinable on the kasra; and the kāf is a particle of address indeclinable on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿قسم﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the overt ḍamma.
﴿لذي﴾: the lām is a preposition indeclinable on the kasra, and dhī is a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is one of the six nouns; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted genitive naʿt (adjective) of ﴿قسم﴾.
﴿حجر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra. Hal and what falls within its scope are the answer to the oath; or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the answer is His saying ﴿إن ربك﴾, or it is omitted and understood, its implied form being "la-nujāziyanna kulla aḥadin bi-mā ʿamil" (We shall surely requite everyone for what he did), or "la-nuʿadhdhibanna" (We shall surely punish).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), a particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and lam is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive, indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿تر﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter.
