﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the place of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿عاد﴾; or in the position of the accusative as standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the meaning being: what deed did your Lord do? ﴿فعل﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿ربك﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿بعاد﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition indeclinable on the kasra, and ʿād is a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) faʿala.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿إرم﴾: a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) from ﴿عاد﴾, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote, on account of being a proper name and feminine.
﴿ذات﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿إرم﴾, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿العماد﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿التي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive as a second adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿إرم﴾.
﴿يخلق﴾: a passive imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the sukūn; mithluhā is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause ﴿لم يخلق﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿في﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿البلاد﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يخلق﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وثمود﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and thamūd is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ʿād, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ثمود﴾.
﴿جابوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿جابوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿الصخر﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿بالواد﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition indeclinable on the kasra, and al-wād is a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the dropped yāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جابوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وفرعون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and firʿawn is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ʿād, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote.
﴿ذي﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿فرعون﴾, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is one of the six nouns.
﴿الأوتاد﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of those mentioned — ʿĀd, Firʿawn and Thamūd; or in the position of the accusative by way of censure (dhamm); or in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being "hum alladhīna ṭaghaw" (they are those who transgressed).
﴿طغوا﴾: a past verb indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, which is dropped to prevent the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿طغوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿في﴾: a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn.
﴿البلاد﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿طغوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿فأكثروا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and aktharū is a past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma; the wāw is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿فيها﴾: fī is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and the pronoun is indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أكثروا﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of ﴿أكثروا﴾.
﴿الفساد﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa. The clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿طغوا﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿فصب﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and ṣabba is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa.
﴿عليهم﴾: ʿalā is a preposition indeclinable on the sukūn, and ﴿هم﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of the genitive; the mīm is a particle of the plural, indeclinable on the sukūn; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿صب﴾.
﴿ربك﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿سوط﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa.
﴿عذاب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra. The clause is conjoined to the clause ﴿طغوا﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating (nāsikh) particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿ربك﴾: the noun (ism) of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa, and the kāf is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿لبالمرصاد﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) is a particle indeclinable on the fatḥa; the bāʾ is a preposition indeclinable on the kasra; and al-mirṣād is a noun in the genitive by the bāʾ, the sign of its genitive being the kasra. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ). The clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason (taʿlīl) for what precedes it.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [Translator's note: the entry begins without quoting the verse; the feminine pronoun in فِيهَا refers to الْبِلادِ.] It is on the feminine of the group, as the plural of balad (land); the masculine is also permissible, meaning by it the plural or the singular.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: [Translator's note: the entry does not quote the word; it evidently refers to سَوْطَ.] It may also be read with ṣād (صوط), because ṭāʾ comes after the sīn.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: Among the best things said about it is that it is figurative (majāz), i.e., He watches over (yarṣudu) the deeds of the servants, i.e., nothing escapes Him. Sufyān said: al-mirṣād is the third bridge of Hell.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسانُ إِذا مَا ابْتَلاهُ رَبُّهُ, i.e., tested him, فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ: concerning the meaning of this and what follows there are two views. The first, which is the view of Qatāda, is that when Allah bestows favour on a person and gives him abundance, he says: "My Lord has honoured me with this", and when He straitens his provision, he says: "He has humiliated me". So Allah rebuked man for this and made known to him that giving him abundance is not out of honouring him, nor is straitening him out of humiliating him. Qatāda said: His honouring him is only through his obedience, and His humiliating him is through his disobedience. The other view is that when Allah gives a person abundance he praises Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and when He straitens him he does not praise Him, so Allah rebuked him, because he must praise Him in both states. The rebuke is in His saying: كَلَّا. What indicates the correctness of the first answer is what comes after the verse: بَلْ لا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ and what follows it, i.e., by this is humiliation, and by its opposite is honour.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: The mafʿūl bihi (direct object) was omitted because the hearer knows it, i.e., "and you do not urge people". Whoever reads تَحَاضُّونَ takes it in the sense of تتحاضّون; one of the two tāʾs was dropped, as in وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا [Āl ʿImrān: 103].

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
The tāʾ (of التراث) is substituted for a wāw (from w-r-th), because it is the closest of the augment letters to it. أَكْلًا is a maṣdar (verbal noun); لَمًّا is its naʿt (adjective).
Al-Farrāʾ said: (لَمًّا means) intense.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: He said: (جَمًّا means) much. Abū Jaʿfar said: كَلَّا — [Translator's note: the text here reads «تماما في كلّ القرآن قال», apparently corrupt; perhaps "it is a complete stop throughout the Qur'an"] — he said: the meaning is: they ought not to be like this, so desist from this deed. إِذا دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا: from Ibn ʿAbbās, i.e., it was shaken; and it (دَكًّا) is an emphatic maṣdar (maṣdar muʾakkid), and likewise the one after it.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا: (الملك) means the angels. صَفًّا صَفًّا is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ: (بجهنم) is in the position of the noun whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); it is also possible that the noun (the deputy agent) is the maṣdar. يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسانُ: the tāʾ may be assimilated into the dhāl. وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرى: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (الذكرى is) repentance; and it has been said: the meaning is, from what direction will the benefit of the remembrance be his?
يَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي: among the Arabs are those who say ليتي, likening it to أنّي. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي, in the Hereafter. Al-Ḥasan said: he knew that there was a life there that has no ending.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
This is the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza, and it is the reading by which the proof has been established through consensus. Al-Kisāʾī read فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ وَلا يُوثِقُ وَثاقَهُ أَحَدٌ [Translator's note: the vowelling printed here is the same as above; al-Kisāʾī's reading is with fatḥa on the dhāl and the thāʾ, i.e., لا يُعَذَّبُ … وَلا يُوثَقُ, passive, as stated below], he said:
And this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, and he argued with two flimsy arguments. One of them is the ḥadīth he claimed from the Prophet ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The ḥadīth does not have a sound chain (isnād). Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd narrated it to us, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Abū ʿUbayd, who said: Hushaym [Translator's note: the text reads «هشام»] and ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbbād narrated to us, from Khālid, from Abū Qilāba, from someone whom the Prophet ﷺ taught to recite: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ. وَلا يُوثِقُ وَثاقَهُ أَحَدٌ with fatḥa on the dhāl and the thāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said: And this ḥadīth is clear [Translator's note: presumably "clearly weak"], because if an unknown person (majhūl) occurs in a ḥadīth it is not used as proof outside the Qur'an, so how much less in the Book of Allah, and in opposition to the community (al-jamāʿa) whose reading is from the Prophet?
His other argument is that the Muslims know that no one on the Day of Resurrection punishes except Allah, so how can it be "no one punishes as He punishes"? This is his argument. Abū Jaʿfar said: He overlooked what the scholars said in the interpretation of the verse, for they said — among them al-Ḥasan —: no one in this world punishes with the like of Allah's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Abū ʿUbayd interpreted the meaning of لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أَحَدٌ as "no one is punished with the punishment of the disbeliever". He was also opposed in this interpretation; among those who opposed him was al-Farrāʾ, who held that the meaning is: no one in this world punishes like the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. There is a third view on it: that a particular man is meant by it.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
It is also permissible to say يا أيّها, because of the vagueness (ibhām) of أيّ. النَّفْسُ is a naʿt (adjective) of أيّ, and الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ is a naʿt of النفس. If you make it a naʿt of أيّ, its accusative is permissible, because the speech has been completed, just as you say: يا زيد الكريم أقبل ("O Zayd, the noble one, come forward").
And the meaning is: (the soul) at rest in Allah's promise, Mighty and Majestic, and His threat.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
ارْجِعِي إِلى رَبِّكِ: concerning its meaning there are two views. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: (return) to your body; so on this view the meaning is that the soul was addressed. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: to Allah; so on this view the address is to the human being, and al-Farrāʾ inclines to this, and to the view that the meaning is that the angels say this to them when they are given their books in their right hands, i.e., return to the reward of your Lord.
فَادْخُلِي فِي عِبادِي (29), i.e., among My righteous servants, i.e., be with them. Al-Farrāʾ said:
"Ibn ʿAbbās alone read «فادخلي في عبدي»". Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a mistake — I mean his saying "alone"; this is the reading of Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Abū Jaʿfar and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Its analysis in Arabic is in the sense of the genus, i.e., let every spirit enter a servant (body); and it has been said: it is a singular that indicates a plural. The mark of the jussive (jazm) in ادخلي, according to the Kufans, is the dropping of the nūn; the Basrans say: it is not declinable (muʿrab), because it is not an imperfect verb and there is no operator with it to put it in the jussive. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the operator in it is the lām (of command), which is omitted.

nahhas-irab:6-7.t:
أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعادٍ (6): He declined عادا fully (with nunation, ṣarf), making it a name of the tribe-kin (al-ḥayy) [Translator's note: the text reads «للحقّ», evidently a misprint for «للحيّ», "for the clan"]; and the reading of al-Ḍaḥḥāk is بِعادٍ without nunation, making it a name of the tribe (qabīla). In the reading of al-Ḥasan, بِعادٍ إِرَمَ, he put عاد into a genitive construct (iḍāfa) with إِرَمَ and did not decline إرم fully.
This verse is problematic for many of the scholars of Arabic. Many people say that إرم is the name of a place, so how can it be a naʿt (adjective) of عاد or a badal (substitute) for it? And it is asked: how is عاد fully declined while إرم is not? Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī [Translator's note: the text reads «القرطبيّ»] claimed that Iram is Alexandria; al-Maqburī said: Iram is Damascus, and likewise Mālik ibn Anas said: "It has reached me that it is Damascus" — Ibn Wahb narrated this from him. Mujāhid said: Iram is "the ancient one", and something other than this has also been narrated from him. From Ibn ʿAbbās: Iram means "the perished", and from Qatāda: Iram is the tribe.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The discussion of this from the side of Arabic is that the clearest view on it is the statement of Qatāda: Iram is a tribe of ʿĀd. As for Iram being Alexandria or Damascus, that is far-fetched, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: وَاذْكُرْ أَخا عادٍ إِذْ أَنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالْأَحْقافِ [al-Aḥqāf: 21]; and al-ḥiqf is sand that has curved and twisted, and neither Damascus nor Alexandria is like that.
It has also been said that إِرَمَ ذاتِ الْعِمادِ is a great city that exists at this time. If this is correct, its summary in grammar is: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعادٍ, the owner of Iram [Translator's note: i.e., with a muḍāf omitted], like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82]. ذاتِ الْعِمادِ is a naʿt of عاد in the sense of the tribe, or of إرم, and likewise.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
In the reading of Ibn al-Zubayr: الَّتِي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مِثْلُها فِي الْبِلادِ [Translator's note: the text gives the standard wording here, though Ibn al-Zubayr's reading is reported elsewhere as «لم يَخْلُق مثلَها», active voice; the explanation that follows assumes the active], meaning: your Lord did not create the like of ʿĀd in the lands, in the greatness of their bodies and their strength; yet that availed them nothing when they opposed the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so He destroyed them.
«وثمود» is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), the implied form being "and with Thamūd". It is a diptote (lam yanṣarif) because it is the name of the tribe; whoever declines it fully makes it the name of the clan (al-ḥayy); and whoever puts it in the genitive without nunation dropped the nunation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. «الذين» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective); it may also be in the position of the accusative with the sense of "I mean", or in the position of the nominative with the sense of "they are those who cut out the rock in the valley". جابوا is from the verbs whose third radical is wāw: jāba al-shayʾa yajūbuhu, when he cuts it and goes into it. And the yāʾ was dropped from الواد [Translator's note: the text reads «من الواو», evidently for «من الوادي/الواد»] because it is the end of a verse, and the kasra indicates it.
وَفِرْعَوْنَ is in the position of the genitive, the meaning being "and with Pharaoh"; it is a diptote because it is a foreign (aʿjamī) name. ذِي الْأَوْتادِ is its naʿt. From Ibn ʿAbbās: ذِي الْأَوْتادِ means "possessor of the armies". Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned other than this concerning it, i.e., possessor of many armies who needed to drive tent-pegs on their journeys.
الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا, i.e., they exceeded the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the lands, i.e., those who were in it.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
[وَالْفَجْرِ is] genitive by the wāw of oath. From Ibn ʿAbbās there are three views on its meaning: among them that it is the dawn of the year, al-Muḥarram; that it is the daytime; and that it is the dawn prayer. As for Masrūq, he said: it is this dawn of yours. He said:
The scholars differed about الفجر: the people of Kufa say it is the whiteness, and the people of Medina say it is the redness. It has been reported from the Arabs: ثوب مشفق and مشفّق, i.e. dyed red.
وَلَيالٍ is conjoined. Its original is ليالي; had it come in its original form, you would say وليالي يا هذا, a diptote, as the poet said: [al-rajaz] 562- قد عجبت منّي ومن يعيليا (She wondered at me and at little Yaʿlā.) They disliked that the weak [final] letter should vary, so the nunation was brought after the yāʾ was dropped, as a compensation for it; it was also said: [a compensation] for the vowel. عَشْرٍ is a naʿt (adjective) of ليال.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
[وَالْوَتْرِ with fatḥa] is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوِتْرِ [with kasra]. [Translator's note: the source prints the second reading as «وَالْوَتْرِ» with fatḥa; the kasra is supplied according to the discussion.] Abū Jaʿfar said: It is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, who argued from several things, among them that it is the more common in people's usage, and that the ḥadīth transmitters say it so. Abū Jaʿfar said:
If someone were to say "the fatḥa is the more common in people's usage", that would be closer [to the truth], even though he has an argument in both — and [there is no argument] in the saying of the ḥadīth transmitters, because the ḥadīth transmitter does not take care over something like this and does not need to take care over it. [Translator's note: the source's «وإن كان له حجة في كليهما ولا في قول المحدثين» seems defective; perhaps «وإن كان لا حجة في كليهما». Rendered as written.] If someone were to say: the fatḥa is preferable because before it is والشفع, which has a fatḥa, he would have said something resembling the [real] arguments. But they are two good dialect forms, as was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq, who said: I read to Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī and Abū Isḥāq al-Ziyādī, from al-Aṣmaʿī, who said: Every single (fard) thing is وتر. The people of the Ḥijāz pronounce الوَتر (odd) with fatḥa and الوِتر (blood-revenge, الذّحل) with kasra; those below them of Qays and Tamīm make them the same. Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Aṣmaʿī has made clear that they are two dialect forms. In the ḥadīth of ʿUmar and Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ: «الذي تفوته صلاة العصر كأنّما وتر أهله وماله» ("Whoever misses the afternoon prayer, it is as though he had been robbed of his family and his wealth"). It may be derived from الوتر in the sense of blood-revenge (الذحل), so that the meaning is "as though he had been despoiled of his family and wealth", by the merit he lost in missing a prayer. One says وتره يتره وترا وترة when he despoiled him, and the noun is الوتر. It may also be derived from الوتر, i.e. single, so that the meaning is "as though his family and his wealth were diminished", i.e. he was left alone (fard). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ singled out the afternoon prayer for this, as has been said, because it was the time of their occupations and their trading, so attending it was hard for them. And He said: حافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَواتِ وَالصَّلاةِ الْوُسْطى [al-Baqara: 238] — the correct view is that it is the afternoon prayer, and that agrees with the ḥadīth.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: [إِذا يَسْرِ:] the original is يسري. The yāʾ was dropped in writing because it is the end of a verse. Whoever keeps it in continuous recitation brings it according to the original, and drops it at the pause in following the Muṣḥaf, which it is not lawful to contradict. That is good because everything paused on loses its case-ending. Among the good things said about the meaning of يسري is: when it advances as the daytime retreats.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: It was said: [هَلْ فِي ذلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ means] "is there [in that] something sufficient?". Among the good things said about it is that the meaning is: Is there in that something by which people of reason swear, magnifying what is sworn by and reinforcing what is sworn to? [Translator's note: the source has «يقسم به … لما أقيم به»; «أقيم» is read as «أقسم», and likewise «يقيمون» below as «يقسمون».] Some scholars inferred from this, and from His magnifying it, that the meaning is "by the Lord of the dawn", because people of reason and faith swear only by Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade anyone to say "by the Kaʿba"; rather, [one should swear] by Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He [Translator's note: the source's «بل خبر عن الله» is unclear; rendered according to the evident sense.], as ʿUmar and Ibn ʿUmar related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers; whoever swears, let him swear by Allah or keep silent.» ʿUmar said: So I have not sworn by it since, neither speaking for myself (ذاكرا) nor relating it from another (آثرا). In another ḥadīth: «Whoever swears by other than Allah has associated partners [with Him] (أشرك)», and in another: «has disbelieved (كفر)». Abū Jaʿfar said: His saying فما حلفت بها is an allusion to the oath (اليمين), which had not been mentioned before, because the hearer knows it. His saying ذاكرا means "saying [it]", as one says ذكر لي فلان كذا ("so-and-so told me such-and-such"), and ولا آثرا means "nor reporting [it]". The meaning of «Whoever swears by other than Allah has associated partners» is: he has done the deed of the polytheists, and likewise "has disbelieved". That is one view. It was also said: فقد أشرك means he has made a partner for Allah in magnification. It was also said: the meaning of «فقد كفر» is "he has covered and concealed the command of Allah", because He commanded that one swear only by Allah.

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(والفجر) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أقسم). (إذا) is an adverb in the position of accusative, stripped of the conditional sense, attached to the omitted verb of the oath. (يسر) is an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, omitted to suit the verse ending.
Clause: « (أقسم) بالفجر ... » has no grammatical position (inceptive).
And the clause: «يسري ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi ... The answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "We shall surely requite every person for what he did" «[Note: some of those who parse made the answer to the oath His words, the Exalted: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصادِ]».

* Morphology:
(3) الشفع: a noun meaning "pair"; it may be figuratively used to mean "creation"; its wazn is فعل «[Note: الشفع has meanings, among them the prayers, the degrees of Paradise, the duality in the attributes of creatures, the Day of Sacrifice, and the ten days of Dhū l-Ḥijja ... and it is said to be Ādam, because he was paired with his wife Ḥawwāʾ.]» with fatḥa and sukūn.
(الوتر) a noun meaning "single"; its wazn is فعل (with fatḥa and sukūn).
(4) يسر: the yāʾ is dropped for lightness, to match the verse endings in the verses and to match the well-known readings.

safi-cedvel:5-5.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) is a particle of interrogation for verification and affirmation (taqrīr). (في ذلك) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (قسم). (لذي) is attached to an naʿt (adjective) of (قسم); the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
Clause: «في ذلك قسم ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).

safi-cedvel:6-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation. (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), its operator being (فعل) «[Note: or in the position of accusative as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), its operator being فعل, i.e. "Have you not seen that your Lord did a mighty deed with ʿĀd ..."]». (بعاد) is attached to (فعل). (إرم) is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) to عاد — or a badal (substitute) for it — genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, as it is a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine. (ذات) is an naʿt (adjective) of إرم, genitive. (التي) is a relative noun in the position of genitive as an naʿt of إرم «[Note: or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it is" (هي), the clause being an explanatory resumptive ... and it may be a direct object of an omitted verb of praise]». (في البلاد) is attached to (يخلق).
Clause: «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «فعل ربّك ... » is in the position of accusative, standing in for the two objects of the heart-verb of seeing, the verb being suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative كيف.
And the clause: «لم يخلق مثلها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (التي)).
(الواو) is a conjunction. (ثمود) is conjoined to عاد, genitive, and is a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of genitive as an naʿt of ثمود — the relative noun being plural following the meaning of ثمود. (بالواد) is attached to (جابوا); the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the omitted yāʾ, omitted to suit the verse endings.
And the clause: «جابوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the relative noun (الذين)).
Verses 10–14: (الواو) is a conjunction. (فرعون) is like ثمود. (ذي) is an naʿt of فرعون, genitive. (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of genitive as an naʿt of فرعون, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the people of Pharaoh" «[Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "they", cut off from the qualification for censure ... and it may be an adjective of ʿĀd, Thamūd and Pharaoh ...]». (طغوا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the implied ḍamma on the alif that was omitted because of the meeting of two silent letters. (في البلاد) is attached to (طغوا). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (فيها) is attached to (أكثروا) «[Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of أكثروا]». (الفاء) is a conjunction. (عليهم) is attached to (صبّ).
And the clause: «طغوا ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين)).
And the clause: «أكثروا» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause طغوا).
And the clause: «صبّ عليهم ربّك ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause أكثروا).
And the clause: «إنّ ربّك لبالمرصاد» has no grammatical position (giving the reason for what precedes).

* Morphology:
(7) إرم: the name of a tribe; it was formerly the name of the grandfather of ʿĀd, so it is a proper name; its wazn is فعل (with kasra then fatḥa).
(العماد) a collective noun (ism jamʿ) meaning lofty buildings, masculine and feminine; its singular is عمادة. One says "so-and-so is tall in al-ʿimād" if his dwelling is known to his visitor, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. In al-Miṣbāḥ: العماد is what something is propped up with — a singular — and its plural is عمد (with two fatḥas); and العماد is lofty buildings, the singular being عمادة. The wazn of العماد is فعال (with kasra on the fāʾ).
(9) جابوا: it contains a weakening by substitution; the original is جوبوا, taken from جاب يجوب; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(11) طغوا: it contains a weakening by omission, by analogy with the verb (تطغوا) — see verse (113) of Sūrat Hūd.
(13) سوط: a non-derived noun meaning a strap of leather made for flogging; it is used in the verse as majāz mursal (unrestricted figurative usage), by the indication of finality or causality.

* Rhetoric:
Istiʿāra makniyya (implicit metaphor): in His words, the Exalted «فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذابٍ».
The punishment is likened, in the speed of its descent, to something poured, and "pouring" is used, which is specific to water. Calling what was sent down a "whip" signals that, great as it was, relative to what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter it is like a whip relative to all the other things with which one is punished.
Istiʿāra tamthīliyya (representational metaphor): in His words, the Exalted «إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصادِ».
Here, His, the Exalted, being the keeper of the deeds of the disobedient, watching them, and requiting even the smallest speck and thinnest membrane of them, so that none escapes Him, glory be to Him, is likened to the state of one who sits on the road lying in wait for whoever passes along it, in order to seize him and do to him what he wishes.

* Benefits:
- (ثمود), a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), is a noun that takes no tanwīn and is put in the genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, except when it is annexed or takes (أل), in which case it is put in the genitive with the kasra.
The nouns that are diptotes can be arranged as follows:
First: those that are diptotes for a single reason, of two kinds:
(a) Those ending in the alif of the feminine, short or extended, such as (ليلى- سلمى- صحراء).
(b) Those of the form of the limit of plurals (muntahā l-jumūʿ), i.e. of the pattern (مفاعل or مفاعيل), which is every plural whose third letter is a redundant alif followed by two letters or by three whose middle one is silent, such as: (مررت بمساجد دمشق).
Second: those that are diptotes for two reasons, of two kinds: proper name and adjective:
(a) As for the proper name, it is a diptote in the following six cases:
1- If it is a feminine proper name.
2- If it is a foreign proper name of more than three letters, such as إدريس- إبراهيم- سقراط. 3- If it is a proper name on the pattern of a verb, such as: (يثرب). 4- If it is a compound by blending (tarkīb mazjī) not ending in (ويه). 5- If it is a proper name on the pattern فعل, such as (عمر). 6- If it is a proper name with alif and nūn added at its end, such as (عثمان). (b) As for the adjective, it is a diptote in the following three cases:
1- If the adjective is on the pattern (أفعل) with feminine فعلاء, such as (أفضل).
2- If the adjective is on the pattern (فعلان) with feminine (فعلى), such as (عطشان، عطشى). 3- If it is an adjective from the following words: such as the word (أخر) as in (فعدة من أيام أخر), and such as the words (مثنى وثلاث)

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive. (أمّا) is a particle of condition and of detailing the states of the human being. (الإنسان) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (ما) is redundant (zāʾida). (الفاء) is a conjunction, and the second is the one linking the apodosis of أمّا. The (نون) in (أكرمن) is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya), which came before the speaker's yāʾ that was omitted to suit the verse ending.
Clause: «أمّا الإنسان ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «الشرط إذا وفعله وجوابه ... » has no grammatical position (parenthetical, with the intention of postponement).
And the clause: «ابتلاه ربّه ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi ... The apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the apodosis of أمّا — which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
And the clause: «أكرمه ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause ابتلاه ربّه.
And the clause: «نعّمه ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause ابتلاه ربّه.
And the clause: «يقول ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الإنسان) «[Note: the original construction: "Whatever happens, the human being says ..."]».
And the clause: «ربّي أكرمن ... » is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «أكرمن ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ربّي).
Verse 16: (الواو) is a conjunction. (أمّا إذا ... أهانن) is parsed like the first, in words and clauses «[Note: note that the clause يقول ... is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو" (he), i.e. the human being ...]». (عليه) is attached to (قدر).

safi-cedvel:17-20.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) is a particle of rebuff and rebuke regarding the preceding idea. (بل) is for transition (iḍrāb intiqālī). (لا) is negative in both places, and one of the two tāʾs is omitted from (تحاضّون). (على طعام) is attached to (تحاضّون). (أكلا) is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative, and likewise (حبّا), which stands in for the maṣdar because it is an ism maṣdar (noun of the verbal noun).
Clause: «لا تكرمون ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «لا تحاضّون ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
And the clause: «تأكلون ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
And the clause: «تحبّون ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).

* Morphology:
(18) تحاضّون: one of the two tāʾs is omitted; the original is تتحاضّون.
(طعام) an ism maṣdar meaning "feeding" (إطعام) from the quadriliteral أطعم; if it means "what is eaten" it is a non-derived noun with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "giving food to the poor".
(19) التراث: a noun for what the dead person leaves as inheritance. It contains the substitution of tāʾ for wāw; the original is الوراث, for lightness of pronunciation, like تجاه and تخمة. Its wazn is فعال (with ḍamma on the fāʾ).
(أكلا) a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral أكل; its wazn is فعل (with fatḥa and sukūn).
(لمّا) a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral لمّ meaning "to gather"; it is used in the verse in the manner of an adjective for intensity, i.e. "abundant gathering".
(20) جمّا: an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral جمّ الشيء (with ḍamma), i.e. "became abundant", of the pattern ضرب; it is also a samāʿī maṣdar of the verb, used as a description for intensity. Its wazn is فعل (with fatḥa and sukūn).

safi-cedvel:21-24.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) is to rebuff the disbelievers from amassing wealth and being miserly with it. (إذا) is an adverb in the position of accusative, attached to the apodosis (يتذكّر). (دكّا) is an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative, and the second is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first, accusative, and likewise (صفّا). (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to a noun of time, accusative — or indeclinable — a badal (substitute) for إذا. (بجهنّم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the verb (جيء). (يومئذ) is an emphasis of the first. (الواو) is circumstantial — or parenthetical. (أنّى) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to the fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذكرى). (له) is attached to the fronted khabar. (يا) is for alerting. (لحياتي) is attached to (قدّمت).
Clause: «دكّت الأرض ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «جاء ربّك- أي أمره-» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause دكّت.
And the clause: «جيء ... بجهنّم» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause دكّت.
And the clause: «يتذكّر الإنسان» has no grammatical position (apodosis of a non-jussive condition).
And the clause: «أنّى له الذكرى ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) — or parenthetical, with no grammatical position.
And the clause: «يقول ... » has no grammatical position (explanatory resumptive) «[Note: or it is a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) of the clause يتذكّر]».
And the clause: «ليتني قدّمت ... » is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «قدّمت ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of ليت.

* Rhetoric:
The art of exaggeration in description (al-ifrāṭ fī l-ṣifa): in His words, the Exalted «وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا». This art is that the speaker mentions a state at which, had he stopped, it would have sufficed, yet he does not stop there until he adds to his speech what is more eloquent in the meaning he intends.
In the noble verse, had He said "in rows" and stopped, that would have sufficed, but He did not stop there; He went beyond it so that the speech would be more eloquent.

* Benefits:
- Omission of the muḍāf noun:
This occurs in the verse we are dealing with (وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ), i.e. "the command of your Lord came". Likewise His words, the Exalted (فَأَتَى اللَّهُ بُنْيانَهُمْ مِنَ الْقَواعِدِ), i.e. "the command of Allah came". Among the omissions of the muḍāf is where a legal ruling is attributed to an entity, since a demand attaches only to actions, as in His words, the Exalted (حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهاتُكُمْ), i.e. enjoyment of them; (حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ), i.e. eating it; (حَرَّمْنا عَلَيْهِمْ طَيِّباتٍ), i.e. partaking of them. Among them also is where the demand is attached to something that has already occurred, as in His words, the Exalted: (أَوْفُوا بِالْعُقُودِ), i.e. with what they contain; (وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ), i.e. with what it requires; and among them (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ الَّتِي كُنَّا فِيها وَالْعِيرَ الَّتِي أَقْبَلْنا فِيها), i.e. the people of the town and the people of the caravan; (وَإِلى مَدْيَنَ أَخاهُمْ شُعَيْباً), i.e. the people of Madyan; (وَكَمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْناها), i.e. the people of a town. Among them also is the maṣdar's standing in for the time, as in our saying:
جئتك طلوع الشمس, i.e. at the time of its rising, and your saying: أفطرت غروب الشمس, i.e. at the time of its setting. But if you said (جئتك مقدم الحاج), here the maṣdar does not stand in for the time, because (مقدم) is a name for the time of arrival.

safi-cedvel:25-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive. (يومئذ) is attached to the negated (يعذّب). (عذابه) is an absolute object standing in for the maṣdar — it is an ism maṣdar — and the pronoun refers to Allah, understood from the context of the verse. (وثاقه) is like عذابه.

Clause: «لا يعذّب ... أحد» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «يوثق ... أحد» has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).

* Morphology:
(وثاقه) is either an ism maṣdar of the quadriliteral أوثق meaning الإيثاق, or a non-derived noun meaning a fetter or a rope; its wazn is فعال (with fatḥa on the fāʾ). See verse (4) of Sūrat al-Qitāl, i.e. (Muḥammad).

safi-cedvel:27-30.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّتها) is an indefinite specified vocative (munādā nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of accusative, and (ها) is for alerting. (النفس) is a badal (substitute) for أيّتها — or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in form. (إلى ربّك) is attached to (ارجعي). (راضية) is an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of ارجعي, and likewise (مرضيّة). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (في عبادي) is attached to (ادخلي), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "among my servants' company".
Clause: «النداء ... » has no grammatical position (resumptive) «[Note: or it is the quoted speech of an implied saying, i.e. "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to the believing soul: O soul ..."]».
And the clause: «ارجعي ... » has no grammatical position (response to the vocative).
And the clause: «ادخلي (الأولى) » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the response to the vocative).
And the clause: «ادخلي (الثانية) » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the response to the vocative).

* Morphology:
(28) مرضيّة: feminine of مرضيّ, a passive participle from the triliteral رضي; its wazn is مفعول. It contains a weakening by substitution: the original is مرضوي — with a yāʾ at the end — the wāw and yāʾ met with the first silent, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into the other yāʾ; then the letter before the yāʾ was given a kasra for harmony.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {والفجر}: the reply to this oath, it has been said, is stated, namely his saying {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لبالمرصاد} [al-Fajr: 14]; Ibn al-Anbārī said this. It has also been said: it is omitted because the meaning indicates it, i.e. "We shall surely requite everyone for what he did", as shown by His enumerating what He did to the bygone generations. Al-Zamakhsharī implied it as "He will surely punish"; he said: "This is indicated by {أَلَمْ تَرَ} [verse 6] up to his saying {فَصَبَّ} [al-Fajr: 13]." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] implied it as what is indicated by the close of the preceding sūra: "their return is surely to Us, and their reckoning is upon Us".
Muqātil said: "«هل» here is in the place of «إنَّ», its implied form being: 'truly in that is an oath for one possessing understanding'; so «هل» on this view is in the position of the reply to the oath." End of quote. This view is false, because it is not fit to be the thing sworn to, even granting that the construction is thus; I have mentioned it only to draw attention to its being unacceptable. It has also been said: there is an omitted muḍāf there, i.e. "and the prayer of the dawn", or "and the Lord of the dawn".
The majority read «الفجر», «الوَتْر» and «يَسْرِ» without tanwīn. Abū al-Dīnār al-Aʿrābī read all three with tanwīn. Ibn Khālawayh said: "This is what is reported of some Arabs, that they pause on the ends of rhymes with tanwīn, even if it is a verb and even if it has the definite article. The poet said:
4558 - أَقِلِّي اللَّوْمَ عاذِلَ والعتابَنْ ... وقُولي إنْ أَصَبْتُ لقد أصابَنْ
(Lessen your blame, O reproacher, and your rebuke; and if I hit the mark, say: he has hit it.)"
By this he means the tanwīn of chanting (tanwīn al-tarannum), which is that when an Arab wishes to abandon chanting — that is, prolonging the voice — he gives the word tanwīn; it occurs only in an unrestricted (muṭlaq) rhyme letter. Some have faulted the grammarians' expression "tanwīn of chanting", saying: rather they ought to call it the tanwīn of abandoning chanting. This tanwīn has another counterpart called "the excessive tanwīn" (al-tanwīn al-ghālī), which is what attaches to a restricted (muqayyad) rhyme letter, as in [the poet's] saying:
4559 -. . . . . . . . . . . . خاوي المخترقْنْ
(… the empty desert-crossing.)
— although some prosodists denied its existence. These two tanwīns have rules differing from the rule of [ordinary] tanwīn, which I have verified in "Sharḥ al-Tashīl", praise be to Allah. The upshot is that this reader treated the verse-endings (fawāṣil) like rhymes and did with them what is done with rhymes. It has parallels, some of which have passed: {الرسولا} [al-Aḥzāb: 66], {السبيلا} [al-Aḥzāb: 67] and {الظنونا} [al-Aḥzāb: 10] in al-Aḥzāb, and {المتعال} in al-Raʿd [verse 9], and «يَسْر» here, as I shall explain, if Allah the Exalted wills. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why are they [the ten nights] indefinite among the things He swore by? I say: because they are particular nights among the genus of nights — the ten being some of them — or particular by a merit not found in others. If you say: why were they not made definite with the lām of prior reference (ʿahd), since they are known nights? I say: had that been said, it would not independently convey the sense of merit that lies in the indefiniteness; and because it is better that the lāms be homogeneous, so that the speech is further from riddling and obscurity." I say: by the homogeneity of the lāms he means that they should all be either for the genus or for prior reference; and the assumption is that the evident view is that the lāms in «الفجر» and what accompanies it are for the genus, so had «الليالي» been brought definite with the lām of prior reference, the homogeneity would have been lost.

semin-durr:2-2.t: The majority read «ليالٍ» with tanwīn, with «عَشْرٍ» as its ṣifa (adjective). Ibn ʿAbbās read «وليالِ عَشْرٍ» with annexation. Some write «ليالِ» in this reading without a yāʾ, and some say «وليالي» with the yāʾ, which is the regular form. It has been said: what is meant is "and the nights of ten days"; on this view it ought to have been said «عشرةٍ», because the thing counted is masculine. The answer is that when the thing counted is omitted, both options are permissible; from this is "and follows it with six (sittin) of Shawwāl", and al-Kisāʾī heard: "We fasted five (khamsan) of the month."

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {والوتر}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with kasra on the wāw, and the rest with fatḥa; they are two dialectal forms, like al-ḥibr and al-ḥabr. The fatḥa is the dialect of Quraysh and those adjacent to them, and the kasra the dialect of Tamīm. These two forms are in «الوتر» as the opposite of al-shafʿ (the even). As for al-witr in the sense of al-tira, i.e. blood-revenge (al-dhaḥl), it is with kasra only; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Al-Aṣmaʿī reported both forms in it as well. Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of Yūnus from him, read it with fatḥa on the wāw and kasra on the tāʾ; this may be a third dialectal form, or he may have transferred the kasra of the rāʾ to the tāʾ, treating joining like pausing.
His saying: {إِذَا يَسْرِ}: accusative through an omitted [verb], namely the verb of the oath, i.e. I swear by it at the time of its travelling by night. Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr dropped the yāʾ of «يَسْري» in pausing and kept it in joining; Ibn Kathīr kept it in both states; and the rest dropped it in both states, because it is absent from the script of the noble Codex. Keeping it is the original, because it is the final radical of an imperfect verb in the nominative; dropping it is in agreement with the Codex and with the verse-heads, and treats the verse-endings like rhymes. Whoever distinguishes between the states of pausing and joining does so because pausing is a place of rest. Attributing night-travel to the night is figurative, since what is meant is "travelling is done in it"; al-Akhfash said this. Someone else said: what is meant is "it diminishes", as in his saying {إِذْ أَدْبَرَ} [al-Muddaththir: 33] and {إِذَا عَسْعَسَ} [al-Takwīr: 17].

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {لِّذِى حِجْرٍ}: al-ḥijr is the intellect; it was discussed before.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {بِعَادٍ إِرَمَ}: the majority read «بعادٍ» as a triptote and «إرَمَ» with kasra on the hamza and fatḥa on the rāʾ and the mīm. «عاد» is originally the name of a man, then applied to the tribe or the clan; it was discussed before. As for «إرَمُ», it has been said: it is the name of a tribe; and it has been said: the name of a city — and the exegetes disagreed in identifying it. If it is the name of a tribe, it is a badal (substitute) or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or accusative through an implied «أعني» (I mean). If it is the name of a city, its parsing in relation to «عاد» is awkward, and it is to be explained by the omission of a muḍāf, as if it were said: "with ʿĀd, the people of Iram"; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is good. It is unlikely to be a badal of inclusion (ishtimāl) from «عاد», since there is no pronoun, and its implied form is awkward. It might be said: since what is meant by ʿĀd is their city — because Iram stands in place of that — the badal is valid. Iram is the name of ʿĀd's grandfather: he is ʿĀd ibn ʿAwaḍ ibn Iram ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ. Zuhayr said:
4560 - وآخَرِين تَرَى الماذيَّ عِدَّتَهْمْ ... مِنْ نَسْجِ داوُدَ أو ما أَوْرَثَتْ إرَمُ
(And others whose equipment you see is gleaming mail of David's weaving, or what Iram bequeathed.)
And Qays al-Ruqayyāt said:
4561 - مَجْداً تليداً بناه أوَّلُوه له ... أَدْرَكَ عاداً وساماً قبلَه إرَما
(Ancient glory which his forebears built for him, reaching back to ʿĀd, and before him to Sām and Iram.)
Al-Ḥasan read «بعادَ» as a diptote. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "Annexed to «إرم»; so «إرَمُ» may be a father, a grandfather or a city." I say: in al-Ḥasan's reading it must be unannexed; rather it is just as it was when it had tanwīn, and «إرمَ» is a badal, or a bayān, or accusative through an implied «أَعْني» [for had it been annexed, it would have had to be a triptote]. «عاد» was made a diptote only out of regard for the sense of "tribe", or it follows one of the two permissible options in «هند» and its class. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, in one transmission, read «بعادَ إرم» as a diptote with fatḥa on the hamza of «أرَمَ». Also from him: «أرْمَ», with fatḥa on the hamza and sukūn on the rāʾ, which is a lightening of «أَرِمَ» with kasra on the rāʾ, a dialectal form of the name of the city; this is the reading of Ibn al-Zubayr. From him, with this reading, «عاد» is reported both as a triptote and as a diptote.
Also from him [al-Ḍaḥḥāk] and from Ibn ʿAbbās: «أَرَمَّ», with fatḥa on the hamza and the rāʾ and the mīm doubled; they made it a past verb. One says: "aramma al-ʿaẓm", i.e. the bone decayed; and also ramma; and someone else armmahu [made it decay]; so afʿala here is both intransitive and transitive. On this reading «ذات» is genitive as a ṣifa (adjective) of «عاد»; and it will then have taken account of its wording at one point, in his saying «أرَمَّ», so no feminine marker was attached, with «أرَمَّ» parenthetical between the adjective and the thing described, i.e. "it decayed", in the sense of "it rotted and perished" — an imprecation against them. Alternatively, the agent of «أرَمَّ» may be a pronoun referring to the Creator, exalted is He, with the object omitted, i.e. "Allah made it decay"; and the imprecatory clause is likewise parenthetical.
And its meaning [was taken account of] at another point, in «ذات», so it was made feminine. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «ومعناها أخرى», apparently with a verb such as «وراعى» dropped; translated according to the evident sense.] It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: «ذاتَ» in the accusative, as the object of «أرَمَّ», with the agent of «أرَمَّ» a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, i.e. Allah the Exalted made it decay; and «أرمَّ» would then be a badal from «فَعَلَ ربُّكَ», or an explanation of it.
Ibn al-Zubayr read «بعادِ أَرِمَ», annexing «عاد» to «أرِم», with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on the rāʾ; it was mentioned that it is the name of the city. It was also read «أرِمِ ذاتِ», annexing «أرم» to «ذات». It is reported from Mujāhid: «أرَمَ», with two fatḥas, the maṣdar (verbal noun) of arima yaʾramu, i.e. perished. On this view it is accusative through «فعَلَ ربُّك» as an accusative of a comparative maṣdar; the implied form is: "how your Lord destroyed [them] with the destruction of the one possessing pillars". This is the strangest of the views.
«ذاتِ العِمادِ»: if it is a ṣifa of a tribe, its meaning is that they were people of tents with poles, with which they moved from place to place; or it is a metonymy for the tallness of their bodies, as in [the poet's] saying:
4562 - رَفيعُ العِمادِ طويلُ النِّجا ... دِ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(High of tent-pole, long of sword-belt …)
— Ibn ʿAbbās said this. If it is a ṣifa of the city, its meaning is that it had columns of stone.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {التي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ}: it may follow [the preceding noun], or be cut off (maqṭūʿ), in the nominative or the accusative. The majority read «يُخْلَقْ» in the passive, with «مِثْلُها» nominative as standing in place of the agent. From Ibn al-Zubayr: «يَخْلُقْ» in the active, with «مثلَها» accusative through it. Also from him: «نَخْلُقْ», with the nūn of majesty.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {وَثَمُودَ}: the majority read it as a diptote, and Ibn Waththāb as a triptote; this was discussed fully before. And «الذين» admits what was said before about {التي لَمْ يُخْلَقْ}. Jāba al-shayʾa yajūbuhu jawban means: he cut it and pierced it. Jubtu al-bilād means: I traversed the lands by travelling. The poet said:
4563 - ولاَ رأَيْتُ قَلوصاً قبلَها حَمَلَتْ ... سِتِّين وَسْقاً ولا جابَتْ بها بلداً
(Never before her did I see a young she-camel that carried sixty camel-loads, or crossed a land with them.)
His saying: {بالواد}: attached either to «جابوا», i.e. in it, or to an omitted [word], as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الصخر», or from the agents. Ibn Kathīr and Warsh kept the yāʾ of «الوادي» in both states — with disagreement from Qunbul: it is reported from him that he kept it in both states, and it is reported from him that he kept it in joining only. The rest dropped it in both states, in agreement with the script of the Codex and out of regard for the verse-endings, as was said before on {إِذَا يَسْرِ} [al-Fajr: 4].

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {الذين طَغَوْاْ}: it admits what was admissible for «الذين» before it: following [the preceding noun] (itbāʿ), or cutting off (qaṭʿ) by way of censure.
His saying: {سَوْطَ}: it is the well-known instrument [the whip]. It has been said: it was called sawṭ because flesh is mixed (yusāṭu) by it when striking, i.e. becomes mixed. Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:
4564 - وَيْلُمِّها خُلَّةً قد سِيْطَ مِنْ دمِها ... فَجْعٌ ووَلْعٌ وإخلافٌ وتبديلُ
(Woe to her mother, what a friend! Into her blood are mixed affliction, lying, breaking of promises and fickleness.)
Another said:
4565 - أحارِثُ إنَّا لو تُساطُ دماؤُنا ... تَزَايَلْنَ حتى لا يَمَسَّ دَمٌ دَما
(O Ḥārith, were our bloods mixed together, they would separate, so that no blood would touch the other.)
It has also been said: it is originally the maṣdar (verbal noun) of sāṭahu yasūṭuhu sawṭan, and then the instrument was named by it. Abū Zayd said: "Their properties among them are sawīṭa", i.e. mixed. The use of "pouring" with "whip" is an eloquent metaphor, and it is common in their speech.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {لبالمرصاد}: al-mirṣād is like al-marṣad, which is the place where the raṣad — plural of rāṣid (watcher), like ḥaras [plural of ḥāris] — are stationed. So al-mirṣād is the pattern mifʿāl from raṣadahu, like mīqāt from waqatahu; al-Zamakhsharī said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed «المِرْصاد» to be an active participle; he said: "As if it were said 'surely by the Watcher', expressed with the intensive form." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] answered him that if it were so, the bāʾ would not enter upon it, since it is not in a position where it may enter, neither as redundant nor as non-redundant. I say: its redundant use in the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ», as in this verse, has occurred in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4566 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإنَّك ممَّا أَحْدَثَتْ بالمُجَرِّبِ
(… for you are, of what [time] has brought about, one who has experienced [it].)
— except that this is poetic licence (ḍarūra), on which ordinary speech is not to be analogised, let alone the most eloquent speech.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {فَأَمَّا الإنسان}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two views on its khabar (predicate). First, which is correct: it is the clause in his saying «فيقولُ», like his saying {فَأَمَّا الذين آمَنُواْ فَيَعْلَمُونَ} [al-Baqara: 26], as was explained before; the adverb [«إذا»] is then accusative through the khabar, because it is intended to come later, and the fāʾ does not prevent that; al-Zamakhsharī and others said this. Second: «إذا» is conditional and its apodosis (jawāb) is «فيقول», his saying «فأَكْرَمَه» is conjoined to «ابتلاه», and the conditional sentence is the khabar of «الإِنسان»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. There is a difficulty in this, because «إمَّا» [Translator's note: so in the text, evidently for «أمَّا»] requires the fāʾ in the clause that occurs as the khabar of what follows it, and it is not omitted except with an implied verb of saying, as in the saying of the Exalted {فَأَمَّا الذين اسودت} [Āl ʿImrān: 106], as was explained before — except under poetic licence.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: with what is his saying «فأمَّا الإِنسانُ» connected? I say: with his saying {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لبالمرصاد}; it is as if it were said: Allah wants nothing from man but obedience; as for man, he does not want that, and nothing concerns him but the immediate [world]." End of quote. He means the connection in terms of meaning, and how this detailing clause was conjoined to what precedes it as following from it. His saying "He wants nothing but obedience" is according to his [Muʿtazilī] doctrine; our doctrine is that Allah wills obedience and other than it, and were it not so, it would not occur. So glory be to Him into whose dominion nothing enters that He does not will. The correction of the expression is to say: "Allah wants from the servant", or "from man", without restriction. Then he said: "If you say: how are his saying {فَأَمَّا الإنسان إِذَا مَا ابتلاه رَبُّهُ} and his saying {وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ابتلاه} balanced, when proper balance requires that the two things occurring after «أمَّا» and «أمَّا» correspond? You say: 'As for man, he is ungrateful; and as for the angel, he is grateful', and 'As for when you do good to Zayd, he does good to you; and as for when you do ill to him, he does ill to you.' I say: they are balanced in that the implied form is: 'and as for him, when his Lord tries him'. That is because his saying {فَيَقُولُ ربي أَكْرَمَنِ} is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is «الإِنسان», and the fāʾ enters because of the sense of condition in «أمَّا»; and the adverb that intervenes between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar is intended to come later, as if He said: 'As for man, he says "my Lord has honoured me" at the time of the trial.' So the second «فيقولُ» must be the khabar of a mubtadaʾ whose implying is necessary."

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ}: Ibn ʿĀmir read it with the dāl doubled, and the rest undoubled; they are two dialectal forms with one meaning, and their meaning is restricting. Of the undoubled form is his saying {الله يَبْسُطُ الرزق لِمَنْ يَشَآءُ وَيَقَدِرُ} [al-Raʿd: 26] and {وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ} [al-Ṭalāq: 7].
His saying: {أَكْرَمَنِ} and «أهانَنِ»: Nāfiʿ read them keeping both their yāʾs in joining and dropping them in pausing, without disagreement from him. Al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr keeps them in both states. From Abū ʿAmr there is disagreement regarding joining: both keeping and dropping are reported from him. The rest drop them in both states; and on dropping is the saying of the poet:
4567 - ومِن كاشِحٍ طاهرٍ عُمْرُه ... إذا ما انْتسَبْتُ له أَنْكَرَنْ
(And of a hidden enemy, outwardly clean all his life, who, when I state my lineage to him, disowns me.)
He means: «أنكرني». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did He not say: 'so He humiliated him and restricted his provision', just as He said: 'so He honoured him and favoured him'? I say: because expansion [of provision] is an honouring from Allah the Exalted of His servant, by bestowing favour on him out of grace without any prior [merit]; but restriction is not a humiliation of him, because failing to bestow grace is not humiliation — just as when Zayd gives you a gift you say: he honoured me; but when he gives you nothing, he is not humiliating you."

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {تُكْرِمُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr read this and the three after it with the yāʾ of the absent person, construing according to the meaning of the "man" mentioned before, since what is meant by it is the genus, and the genus has the sense of a plural. The rest read all of them with the tāʾ, addressing "man", by which the genus is meant, by way of shift of person (iltifāt). The Kufans read «تَحاضُّون», the original being tataḥāḍḍūn, with one of the two tāʾs omitted, i.e. you do not urge one another. It is reported from al-Kisāʾī: «تُحاضُّون» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, which is the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿAlqama, i.e. you do not urge your own selves. The rest read «تَحُضُّون», from ḥaḍḍahu ʿalā kadhā, i.e. he incited him to it; its object is omitted, i.e. you do not urge yourselves nor others. It is also possible that nothing is implied, i.e. you do not engage in urging.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {على طَعَامِ}: attached to «تحاضُّون». «طعام» may be in its original sense, a noun for what is eaten, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. to giving, or to providing, food; or it may be a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) in the sense of iṭʿām (feeding), like al-ʿaṭāʾ in the sense of al-iʿṭāʾ, in which case there is no omission. The tāʾ in «التراث» replaces a wāw, because it is from al-wirātha (inheritance); similar are tawlaj, tawrāh and tukhama; this was discussed before. «لَمَّاً» means gathered. One says: lamamtu al-shayʾa lamman, i.e. I gathered it together. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
4568 - إذا كان لَمَّاً يَتْبَعُ الذَّمَّ ربَّه ... فلا قَدَّس الرحمنُ تلك الطَّواحِنا
(If [eating] is a gobbling-up that brings blame upon its owner, then may the Merciful not bless those molars.)
And lamamtu shaʿathahu (I set right his disorder) is from that. Al-Nābigha said:
4569 - ولَسْتَ بمُسْتَبْقٍ أخالً لا تَلُمُّه ... على شَعَثٍ، أيُّ الرِّجالِ المهذَّبُ
(You will not keep a brother whom you do not take as he is, despite his faults; which man is free of flaws?)
Al-jamm means much. From it comes jummat al-māʾ (the gathered mass of water). Zuhayr said:
4570 - فلمَّا وَرَدْنَ الماءَ زُرْقاً جِمامُه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When they came down to the water, its full pools clear blue …)
And from it is al-jumma for [a mass of] hair, and their saying "they came al-jammāʾ al-ghafīr (all together, in a great throng)" is from that.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {دَكّاً دَكّاً}: there are two views on it. First: it is an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), and the second «دكاً» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, a verbal (lafẓī) emphasis; Ibn ʿUṣfūr said so, but the meaning is not according to that. Second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being: with the pounding repeated upon it, as in "I taught him arithmetic chapter by chapter"; this is the evident meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's statement. Likewise «صَفَّاً صَفَّاً» is also a ḥāl, i.e. standing in rows, or in many rows.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: accusative through «جيْء», and what stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is «بجهنَّمَ». Makkī allowed «يومَئِذٍ» to stand in place of the agent. As for the second «يومَئذ», it has been said: it is a badal (substitute) from «إذا دُكَّت», and what governs both is «يتذكَّر»; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and this is the doctrine of Sībawayh, namely that what governs the replaced noun governs the badal; while the doctrine of others is that the badal is on the intention of repeating the governing word. It has also been said: what governs «إذا دُكَّتْ» is «يقولُ», and what governs «يومئذ» is «يتذكَّر»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this.
His saying: {وأنى لَهُ الذكرى}: «أنَّى» is a fronted khabar (predicate), «الذكرى» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and «له» is attached to what the adverb is attached to.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {لاَّ يُعَذِّبُ}: al-Kisāʾī read «لا يُعَذَّبُ» and «لا يُوْثَقُ» in the passive, and the rest read both in the active. As for al-Kisāʾī's reading, the verb in it is ascribed to «أحد», and the agent is omitted because it is known, namely Allah the Exalted, or the Zabāniya (angel-guards) who carry out the torment by the command of Allah the Exalted. As for «عذابه» and «وثاقه», the two maṣdars (verbal nouns) may be annexed to the agent, with the pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, or annexed to the object, with the pronoun referring to man; and «عذاب» occurs in the place of taʿdhīb (tormenting). The meaning is: no one will be tormented with a tormenting like Allah the Exalted's tormenting of this disbeliever, and no one will be bound with a binding like Allah's binding of him with chains and fetters; or: no one will be tormented like the tormenting of the disbeliever, nor bound like his binding, because of his disbelief and obstinacy. So al-wathāq is in the sense of al-īthāq, like al-ʿaṭāʾ in the sense of al-iʿṭāʾ. However, on making the noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar) govern as what it names [the maṣdar] governs, there is a confused disagreement: disallowance is reported from the Basrans and allowance from the Kufans, and the reverse has been reported from both parties. Of its governing is [the poet's] saying:
4571 - أكُفْراً بعد رَدِّ الموتِ عني ... وبعد عَطائِكَ المِئَةَ الرَّتاعا
(Is it ingratitude, after you warded off death from me, and after your giving me the hundred grazing camels?)
Whoever disallows it makes «المِئَة» accusative through an implied verb. More explicit than this is the saying of another:
4572 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإنَّ كلامَها شفاءٌ لِما بيا
(… for speaking to her is a cure for what ails me.)
It has also been said: the meaning is: no one will bear the torment of man, as in his saying {وَلاَ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أخرى} [al-Anʿām: 164]; al-Zamakhsharī said this. As for the reading of the rest, the verb is ascribed to its agent.
The pronoun in «عذابَه» and «وَثاقَه» may refer to the Creator, exalted is He, meaning: no one in this world torments like the torment of Allah the Exalted on that day, i.e. the torment of whoever torments in this world is not like the torment of Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection; Abū ʿAbd Allāh said so. There is a difficulty in this, in that it would entail «يومئذٍ» being governed by the comparative maṣdar, which is impossible since it precedes it — unless it be said that latitude is allowed with it [the adverb].
It has also been said: the meaning is: He does not entrust His torment or His binding to anyone, because the matter in that belongs to Allah alone. It has also been said: the meaning is that in severity and horror it is in a realm such that no one has ever tormented in this world like it. This was rejected on the ground that when «لا» enters the imperfect it makes it future, and if it is future it does not fit this meaning, and it is not applied to the past except by a far-fetched figure; and on the ground that what is meant by «يومَئذٍ» is the Day of Resurrection, not the abode of this world. It has also been said: the meaning is that no one in this world torments like Allah's tormenting of the disbeliever in it [the world]; but this is rejected by what the preceding one was rejected by. The pronoun may also refer to man, meaning: none of the Zabāniya of torment torments [anyone] as they torment this disbeliever; or the meaning is: no one bears the torment of man, as in his saying {وَلاَ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أخرى} [Fāṭir: 18]. These views are hard to attain for whoever seeks them elsewhere than in this place, because they are scattered elsewhere and difficult to extract from there.
Nāfiʿ in one transmission, and Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba, with disagreement reported from them, read «وِثاقَه» with kasra on the wāw.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {ياأيتها}: this is the reading of the majority, «يا أيتُها», with the feminine tāʾ. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يا أيُّها», like the vocative of the masculine; no one allowed this except the author of "al-Badīʿ", and this [reading] is evidence for him. It has a rationale: just as it does not agree with its ṣifa (adjective) in dual and plural, it may not agree with it in feminine gender; you say: yā ayyuhā al-rajulān, yā ayyuhā al-rijāl. «راضيةً» and «مَرْضيَّةً» are two ḥāls (circumstantials), i.e. combining the two descriptions, because neither of them entails the other.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {فِي عِبَادِي}: it may mean: into the body of My servants; and the meaning may be: among the company of My servants. Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima and a group read «في عبدي», meaning the genus. The first verb is made transitive with «في» because the adverbial sense is not literal, as in "I entered into (fī) the throng of people", and the second is transitive by itself because the adverbial sense is real — so it has been said. This only works on one of the two views, namely that what is meant by "the soul" is one of the believers, and that it is a command to enter among the company of His servants; but if what is meant by the soul is the spirit, and that it is commanded to enter into the bodies, then the adverbial sense is real in it too.

ukberi-tibyan:1-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْفَجْرِ (١) وَلَيَالٍ عَشْرٍ (٢) وَالشَّفْعِ وَالْوَتْرِ (٣) وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَسْرِ (٤)).
The answer of the oath is (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ).
(وَالْوَتْرِ): with fatḥa and with kasra [on the wāw], two dialectal forms. (إِذَا) is an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is omitted, i.e. «أُقْسِمُ بِهِ إِذَا يَسْرِي» (I swear by it when it passes). The better [reading] is to keep the yāʾ; and whoever omits it does so for the sake of agreement with the verse-endings.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا فِي الْبِلَادِ (١١)).
The words of the Exalted (الَّذِينَ طَغَوْا): regarding the plural there are two aspects; the first of them is that it is an adjective (ṣifa) for the whole group [ʿĀd, Thamūd and Pharaoh].
The second: it is an adjective for Pharaoh and his followers, and mentioning him sufficed for mentioning them.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَمَّا الْإِنْسَانُ إِذَا مَا ابْتَلَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأَكْرَمَهُ وَنَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ (١٥)).
The words of the Exalted (فَأَكْرَمَهُ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (ابْتَلَاهُ).
As for «فَيَقُولُ», it is the answer of «إِذَا»; and «إِذَا» together with its answer is a khabar (predicate) about «الْإِنْسَانُ».

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ عَلَى طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ (١٨)).
The words of the Exalted (وَلَا يَحُضُّونَ): the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. «لَا يَحُضُّونَ أَحَدًا» (they do not urge anyone), i.e. they do not urge themselves. It is also read (وَلَا تَحَاضُّونَ), which is an intransitive verb, in the sense of «تَتَحَاضُّونَ» (you urge one another).

ukberi-tibyan:22-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَ رَبُّكَ وَالْمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا (٢٢) وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الْإِنْسَانُ وَأَنَّى لَهُ الذِّكْرَى (٢٣) يَقُولُ يَالَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِي (٢٤))
The words of the Exalted (يَوْمَئِذٍ): it is a badal (substitute) for «إِذَا» in the words of the Exalted (إِذَا دُكَّتِ), and what governs it is «يَتَذَكَّرُ».
(يَقُولُ) is an explication of «يَتَذَكَّرُ».
It is also permissible that what governs «إِذَا» be «يَقُولُ», and what governs «يَوْمَئِذٍ» be «يَتَذَكَّرُ». (صَفًّا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:25-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لَا يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُ أَحَدٌ (٢٥) وَلَا يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُ أَحَدٌ (٢٦) يَا أَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ (٢٧) ارْجِعِي إِلَى رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً (٢٨)).
The words of the Exalted (لَا يُعَذِّبُ) and (لَا يُوثِقُ): both are read with kasra on the dhāl and the thāʾ, and the fāʿil (agent) is «أَحَدٌ»; and the hāʾ refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
And both are read with fatḥa, as verbs whose agent is not named (passive), and the hāʾ is an object; the implied form is «مِثْلُ عَذَابِهِ» (the like of his punishment) and «مِثْلُ وَثَاقِهِ» (the like of his binding). «الْعَذَابُ» and «الْوَثَاقُ» are nouns for «التَّعْذِيبُ» (punishing) and «الْإِيثَاقُ» (binding).
(رَاضِيَةً) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:6-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ (٦) إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ (٧)).
(إِرَمَ) is a diptote because of definiteness and femininity. It is said that it is the name of a tribe; on this view the implied form is «إِرَمَ صَاحِبُ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ» (Iram, the possessor of [the city] of the pillars), because «ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ» is a city.
It is also said that (ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ) is a description, as you say: «الْقَبِيلَةُ ذَاتُ الْمُلْكِ» (the tribe possessing sovereignty).
It is also said that «إِرَمَ» is a city; on this view the implied form is «بِعَادٍ صَاحِبِ إِرَمَ» (with ʿĀd, the possessor of Iram).
It is also read «بِعَادِ إِرَمَ» with annexation (iḍāfa), so no implied form is needed. And it is read «إِرَمَ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ» in the genitive by annexation. [Translator's note: so in the printed text; the reading meant is apparently «إِرَمِ ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ», with «إِرَمِ» annexed to «ذَاتِ الْعِمَادِ».]

ukberi-tibyan:9-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جَابُوا الصَّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ (٩) وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الْأَوْتَادِ (١٠)).
(ثَمُودَ) is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «عَادٍ», and likewise «فِرْعَوْنَ».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Fajr
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والفَجْرِ﴾: ”اَلْفَجْرُ“ is the breaking forth of the morning from the night. The answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالمِرْصادِ﴾ [al-Fajr: 14] ("your Lord is surely ever watchful").

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَلَيالٍ عَشْرٍ﴾ ("and ten nights"): the nights of the ten [days] of Dhū al-Ḥijja.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿والشَّفْعِ والوَتْرِ﴾ ("by the even and the odd"): it was read ”والوَتْرِ“ with fatḥa on the wāw. And the even (al-shafʿ) is the Day of Sacrifice, and the odd (al-watr) is the Day of ʿArafa [Translator's note: the source reads «والوَتْرُ يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ، والوَتْرُ يَوْمُ عَرَفَةَ», i.e. "al-watr" twice; the first is evidently «الشَّفْعُ»]. And it was said: the even and the odd are the numbers, and all numbers are either even or odd. And it was said: ”اَلْوَتْرُ“ is Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, the One, and ”اَلشَّفْعُ“ is all of creation, created in pairs.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا يَسْرِ﴾ ("and by the night when it passes"): when it goes by; ”سَرى، يَسْرِي“ [is the verb], just as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذْ أدْبَرَ﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 33] ("and by the night when it departs"). And in ﴿يَسْرِ﴾ the yāʾ was omitted because it is the end of a verse (raʾs āya). It was also read: ”واللَّيْلِ إذا يَسْرِي“ with the yāʾ retained. Following the Muṣḥaf and omitting the yāʾ is dearer to me, because the reading with it is more widespread, and verse-endings are pauses (fawāṣil) with which the yāʾs are omitted, the kasras indicating them.

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ في ذَلِكَ قَسَمٌ لِذِي حِجْرٍ﴾: that is, for one possessed of intellect and understanding. The meaning of the oath is the emphasis of what is mentioned and its confirmation by swearing upon it.

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعادٍ﴾ ("have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd?"): it was said: they are two ʿĀds, the first ʿĀd, which is Iram, and the later ʿĀd. And it was said: Iram is the father of ʿĀd, he being ʿĀd ibn Iram. And it was said: Iram is the name of their town in which they lived. Iram is a diptote (lam tanṣarif, not fully declined) because it was made the name of the tribe; therefore it takes fatḥa while being in the position of the genitive (fī mawḍiʿ jarr).

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿ذاتِ العِمادِ﴾: that is, possessed of tallness; one says ”رَجُلٌ مُعَمَّدٌ“ when a man is tall. And it was said: ﴿ذاتِ العِمادِ﴾ means possessed of tall, lofty buildings.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿وَثَمُودَ الَّذِينَ جابُوا الصَّخْرَ بِالوادِ﴾: ”جابُوا“ means "they cut", just as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الجِبالِ بُيُوتًا فارِهِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 149] ("and you hew houses out of the mountains with skill").

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَفِرْعَوْنَ ذِي الأوْتادِ﴾ ("and Pharaoh, possessor of the stakes"): ”فِرْعَوْنَ“ is a diptote (lam yanṣarif) because it is foreign. And it was said ﴿ذِي الأوْتادِ﴾ because he had four pillars; when he punished a person he tied each of his limbs to one of those pillars. Its meaning is: "Have you not seen how your Lord destroyed these nations that denied their messengers?! And how He made their penalty that He made the punishment His whip with which He struck them?!" So He said: ﴿فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذابٍ﴾ [al-Fajr: 13] ("so your Lord poured upon them a whip of punishment").

zajjaj:14-14.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِالمِرْصادِ﴾: that is, He lies in wait with punishment for whoever disbelieves in Him and worships another.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأمّا الإنْسانُ إذا ما ابْتَلاهُ رَبُّهُ فَأكْرَمَهُ ونَعَّمَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أكْرَمَنِ﴾. The meaning is: "When his Lord tests him and gives him ample provision, he says: my Lord has honoured me."
﴿وَأمّا إذا ما ابْتَلاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أهانَنِ﴾ [al-Fajr: 16]: that is, He made his provision measured (restricted). ﴿فَيَقُولُ رَبِّي أهانَنِ﴾ [al-Fajr: 16] ﴿كَلا﴾ [al-Fajr: 17]: that is, the matter is not as the human being supposes. By this the unbeliever who does not believe in the Resurrection is meant: for him honour and humiliation are only by having a large share in this world; whereas the characteristic of the believer is that honour, for him, is Allah's granting him success (tawfīq), that is, what leads him to a share in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:17-18.t: ﴿كَلا بَلْ لا تُكْرِمُونَ اليَتِيمَ﴾ ﴿وَلا تَحاضُّونَ عَلى طَعامِ المِسْكِينِ﴾ ("nay, but you do not honour the orphan, nor do you urge one another to feed the poor"). It is also read: ”وَلا تَحُضُّونَ عَلى طَعامِ المِسْكِينِ“ ("nor do you urge [others] to feed the poor"). They used to devour the property of orphans wastefully and hastily, so He said: ﴿وَتَأْكُلُونَ التُّراثَ أكْلا لَمًّا﴾ [al-Fajr: 19] ("and you devour the inheritance, devouring it entirely"), that is, the inheritance of orphans. ”لَمًّا“: they gather up all of it.

zajjaj:20-20.t: And His saying: ﴿وَتُحِبُّونَ المالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا﴾: that is, abundantly. And ”اَلتُّراثُ“: its original form is ”اَلْوُراثُ“, from ”وَرِثْتُ“ ("I inherited"); but tāʾ substitutes for wāw when the wāw has ḍamma, as in ”تُراثٌ“, whose original form is ”وُراثٌ“, and as in ”تُجاهٌ“, whose original form is ”وُجاهٌ“, from ”واجَهْتُ“ ("I faced").

zajjaj:21-21.t: And His saying: ﴿كَلا إذا دُكَّتِ الأرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا﴾: when it is shaken by earthquake and part of it pounds part of it.

zajjaj:22-22.t: ﴿وَجاءَ رَبُّكَ والمَلَكُ صَفًّا صَفًّا﴾ ("and your Lord comes, and the angel(s), rank upon rank"): the meaning is ”والمَلائِكَةُ“ ("and the angels"), just as He, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا أنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ في ظُلَلٍ مِنَ الغَمامِ والمَلائِكَةُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 210] ("do they await anything but that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels?").

zajjaj:23-23.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَجِيءَ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِجَهَنَّمَ﴾ ("and Hell is brought, that Day"), as He said: ﴿وَبُرِّزَتِ الجَحِيمُ لِلْغاوِينَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 91] ("and Hellfire will be brought into view for the deviators"). And it was said in the exegesis: Hell will be brought, led by a thousand reins, each rein in the hands of seventy thousand angels.
﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَذَكَّرُ الإنْسانُ﴾: on that Day the human being will display repentance. ﴿وَأنّى لَهُ الذِّكْرى﴾: that is, and from where will he have the remembrance? That is: the repentance.

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿يَقُولُ يا لَيْتَنِي قَدَّمْتُ لِحَياتِي﴾ ("he will say: would that I had sent ahead for my life!"): that is, for the abode of the Hereafter, in which there is no death.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ”فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لّا يُعَذَّبُ عَذابَهُ أحَدٌ“ (passive reading: "so on that Day none will be punished with his punishment"): the meaning is: "No one will be punished with the punishment of this unbeliever, and the punishment of this class of unbelievers", ﴿وَلا يُوثِقُ وثاقَهُ أحَدٌ﴾ ("and none will bind as he binds"). And whoever read ﴿لا يُعَذِّبُ﴾ [al-Fajr: 25] (active), and that is the reading of the majority, then the meaning is: "No one will undertake Allah's punishment on the Day of Resurrection; the dominion on that Day belongs to Allah alone, Majestic and Mighty is He." And it was said: ”لا يُعَذِّبُ عَذابَهُ أحَدٌ“ means: [no one punishes with] the punishment of Allah; so on this view no one in this world punishes with [the like of] Allah's punishment in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying: ﴿يا أيَّتُها النَّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنَّةُ﴾ ("O tranquil soul"): ”أيُّ“ is put in the feminine when you call a feminine with it, and it may also be put in the masculine: you say ”يا أيَّتُها المَرْأةُ“ ("O woman"), or if you wish ”يا أيُّها المَرْأةُ“. Whoever puts it in the masculine does so because ”أيُّ“ is vague (mubham); and whoever puts it in the feminine does so because, despite its vagueness, inflection (iʿrāb) and annexation (iḍāfa) have become attached to it. And Sībawayh claimed that some Arabs say ”كُلْتُهُنَّ“ for ”كُلُّهُنَّ“ ("all of them [fem.]"). And ”اَلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ“ is the one that has found tranquillity in faith and humbled itself before its Lord.

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿ارْجِعِي إلى رَبِّكِ راضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً﴾ ("return to your Lord, well pleased and well pleasing"): the original form of ﴿مَرْضِيَّةً﴾ is ”مَرْضُوَّةً“; that is, pleased with what He has given it; it has become pleased and been purified.

zajjaj:29-29.t: ﴿فادْخُلِي في عِبادِي﴾ ("so enter among My servants"): among the company of My chosen servants. It was also read: ”فادْخُلِي في عَبْدِي“ ("so enter into My servant") ﴿وادْخُلِي جَنَّتِي﴾ [al-Fajr: 30] ("and enter My Paradise"). On this reading — and Allah knows best — [the meaning is]: "Enter to your companion from whom you went out, so enter into him." But most of the reading and the exegesis is: ﴿فادْخُلِي في عِبادِي﴾ ﴿وادْخُلِي جَنَّتِي﴾ [al-Fajr: 30].
